entities.role: general secretary, Rangamati District Sports Association

posts.summary: Long article on Rangamati district sports: the golden age is gone, the handball league has not been held for 15 years and the football second division is closed for over 12 years, blamed on political conflict and lack of sponsorship; the 2013-14 football league cost 35 lakh taka funded by the Chittagong Hill Tracts Development Board, while BFF's grants were only 3 lakh per district and not even paid in full.
The poster's dream: lose 2-0 to Australia away and beat Jordan 2-1.
What murky water is being stirred over Reasat? If you do not want to say it in the group, tell me in the inbox.
Fan asks at what time tomorrow's Bangladesh vs Bhutan match is in Bangladesh time.
Fan asks if the U19 match is today and which channel will show it.

Kaler Kantho interview with Sarowar Jaman Nipu, SAFF U16 best player: he could not join BKSP for lack of money, missed the final through suspension, scored two against Sri Lanka and a penalty against India, and trained at Bhuiyan Academy 35 km from home for 50 taka a day; he now dreams of the senior Bangladesh team.

Finally, information on Sheikh Jamal's other foreign player: Chidozie Johnson, 32, Nigerian defender, who played for Abia Warriors, Lobi Stars, Heartland and Enyimba Aba, with 8 CAF Champions League matches and 2 goals plus 1 CAF Super Cup match.
SAFF U19 Championship: Afghanistan 1-0 Maldives.

BFF announced the 23-member Bangladesh squad for the Australia and Malaysia matches: goalkeepers Sohel, Russell and Rana; defenders Nasir Chowdhury, Raihan, Munna, Linkon, Yeasin, Topu, Meshu and Nasir; midfielders Mamun, Sohel, Jamal, Zahid, Imon, Raju and Hemanta; forwards Emily, Enamul, Toklis, Komol and Jewel; Abahani goalkeeper Zia missed out despite a good league season, and Raju got in without playing a league match.

Profile of Johnson Chidozie, a former student of Kruif: Nigerian defender born 6 March 1983, with clubs including Wikki Tourist, Enyimba, Akwa United, Sunshine, Heartland, Lobi Stars and Abia Warriors, plus Super Eagles and CAF Champions League honours.

Sarcastic post: there is no syndicate in BFF, that is why Reasat did not get a chance in the team, but some get into the 23-member squad without playing any league match; let Australia send us 7 or 8 goals, it will feel good.
Bare link to a Socceroos Facebook post.

Newspaper report on the 23-member Bangladesh squad for the World Cup and Asia Cup qualifiers: Toklis Ahmed's return after a season on the bench is the only surprise, while Premier League six-goal scorer Tawhidul Alam Sabuz and Sheikh Russel defender Rezaul Reza missed out; Sheikh Jamal supplies 11 players; coach Kruif says the squad was chosen on tactical grounds.
Tomorrow, there is nothing to worry about regarding Bhutan; the poster will be disappointed if Bangladesh cannot give Bhutan four.
Imagined Bangladesh vs Australia counter: Hemanto carries the ball and passes to Zahid, who dribbles through a player and puts in a low cross, and Emily or Enamul touches it in for the goal.
On 16 September the SAFF 2015 group draw will be finalised in Delhi.
Australia vs Bangladesh: just one draw is wanted; a draw away means stopping Australia in the home leg at Bangabandhu National Stadium with home support is possible; dare to dream.

Poster asks what others understood from the article about the AFC Cup format, arguing Pakistanis understand nothing about it; if two teams in the East is no problem, then 5 matches and 4 rounds to qualify is harder than the AFC Champions League, and if the club licensing criteria are true, how did last year's Laos club and this year's Afghan club play?
Fan asks whether the U19 match is shown on ATN.

Poster wants a 3v3 practice match on Kamalapur turf, Reasat Akmal and Rabbi against Wedson, Walson and Emeka Darlington, so that when the first side thrashes the foreigners everyone will understand whether there is a syndicate or not.
Fan asks someone to share a photo or video of Kamalapur Stadium, as his heart is eager to see it.

It is not just a tournament, it is a place to prove yourself: two Liverpool scouts, Dave Rogers and Michael William Rice, are in Nepal scouting for their academy; the poster believes Masuk, Mannaf and Ibrahim will impress them and predicts 5-0 today.
Bangladesh vs Bhutan, formation 4-3-3, line-up Rohmot, Badsha, Emon, Salahuddin, Bappy, Jonny, Bipul, Rohit, Mannaf, Rakine; prediction 5-0.

Poster saw a live Jamuna TV programme with the BD team captain and coach, who said they had only 20 days and did not take much pressure; the 16-year-old boys practised on dal-bhat and suffered a lot, the coach said.

The coach accepted defeat, maybe he is a realist, but the poster wants Bangladesh to give the Aussies a run for their lives and play quality football instead of clustering the defence; his preferred XI is Shahidul; Raihan, Topu, Yeasin, Munna; Jahid, Jamal, Mamun, Jewel; Vincent, Toklis, with Sohel Rana, Enamul/Emily and Nasir/Meshu as second-half subs.

Footballer development needs supporter development too, the poster argues: stone-age mentality says one bad league match makes a player unfit for the national team, when a player fitting the national team profile may not play well in the league; saying 'isn't it' is not constructive criticism.
Post shares a FIFA link about club licensing going global by the end of 2016.
What is Afghanistan's story? They left SAFF, so why SAFF U16 and U19? The poster does not understand.
On 20 September, Atletico de Kolkata should have been brought to Dhaka and sized up.
Fan asks what the Nepali language is and says it seems to have many similarities with Sanskrit.
Live-match comment: Mannaf offside.
Why does Mannaf fall in offside so much? But after the first 10 minutes the poster is back to the game.
Fan asks how much mobile data it could cost to watch the whole match.
Bangladesh youth are playing back passes very well.
What rubbish did they play? No pace, no plan; Titu coach is of no class; lollipop football against Bhutan.
Live-match goal celebration post: GOAL.

Poster cannot believe what Bangladeshi TV channels and BFF are doing: they do not even have to produce it themselves, and even Nepal, in its current situation, did not neglect the tournament; the media should have learned from U16 what people want.
Ibrahim, Mannaf and Tutul: the poster believes they will impress Dave and Michael.
Chelsea of the SAFF U19 championship is our Bangladesh.
A 2-goal win, not bad as a preparation match.
Bangladesh 8, Bhutan 2, oh wait, the poster is talking about offsides.
SAFF U19 Championship, full time: Bangladesh 2-0 Bhutan; if coach Titu had not parked the bus it would have been 4-0, but Bangladesh are still in the semi-final.
SAFF U19 Championship 2015: Bangladesh 2-0 Bhutan; respect from Nepal.
GTV can show English Premier League matches but seems ashamed to broadcast their own country's matches.

Apart from missed goals, the poster has no tension about this balanced team; Mannaf will adapt to international matches soon, a good foreign coach is needed and De Kruif should stay for the AFC tournament; Bhutan are getting a good generation, and so are Bangladesh.
Champions Sheikh Jamal ended the league with a win, beating Dhaka Abahani 2-1 in the last match; Abahani finished 4th, Sheikh Russel runners-up and Mohammedan 3rd.
Fan post asking Arif Faisal bro whether he will turn on Abahani's history channel.
Duplicate post: Soccer League will buy the BPL for one million pounds, winter timing, four host cities and live TV broadcast; BFF must agree quickly or there is no deal.

Soccer League will buy the BPL for one million pounds; from next season the BPL will be in winter, four cities will host matches, and matches will be broadcast live on TV; BFF must agree Soccer League UK's terms quickly or there is no deal.
Two-word post: as I was saying.

Sarcastic post: the poster does not like Titu, so he is foolish, and Titu is the best coach in the country's football history; Wales U19 players are not worthy of the national team because Titu is the coach.

Long post praising Kazi Salahuddin for opposing the franchise league from the start and criticising the ISL as SAFF president, saying no country developed football through a franchise league; the BPL, unprofitable under BFF, is now sold for a million pounds, and Soccer League UK will make it thrive.
Poster says after warming the bench at Sheikh Jamal all year for a fat amount, if you still get a national team chance, then Sheikh Jamal is good; why would Toklis leave the club?
Fan asks what a franchise league is and what happens if it joins the BPL.

BFF demanded 12.2 crore for the Premier League and Soccer League agreed with conditions (four cities, league before winter, holiday scheduling, all matches on TV); poster is happy with the proposal and says BFF can now threaten the big clubs.
Fan asks where and when the U16 AFC trial will be.
Fan asks if there is any football academy in Chittagong for practice or coaching and asks for suggestions.
AFC U16 match dates: Bangladesh U16 vs Saudi Arabia U16 on 16 September 2015 and vs UAE U16 on 18 September 2015.
First SAFF U19 Championship: India 2-0 Afghanistan; poster wonders how, since India supposedly sent a second-string team, and notes everyone fears Afghanistan after they beat Maldives.

Poster says football needs a popular league with matches outside Dhaka, using district stadiums, and a rule of at most three foreigners per team with no two foreigners in the same position, so local strikers get their chances.

Poster proposes BFF keep Bangladesh A and B teams alongside the national team, so dropped players can sharpen their performance and young U18/U16 talents can be contracted, with regular practice matches against big clubs and foreign age-group teams.

Poster proposes six venues instead of four so every two teams have a home venue, and suggests keeping Bangabandhu Stadium closed next season for maintenance and preparing it for the BSSL or only international matches, using Kamalapur instead.
Cryptic post: that is ownership, not sponsorship, with a Facebook story link.

Poster lists the Fed Cup 2015 and BPL 2014-15 top scorers (Emeka 19, Wedson 17, Bangoura 17, Augustine 15, Enamul 13) to argue that to get a Bangladesh call-up you do not need to perform: automatic choice theory rules, Enamul for the bench and Emily for the national team.
Poster asks why Aminur Rahman Sajib.
Teaser post: readers have learned about the syndicate by now, and now they will learn about the 'packet'; details coming.
Poster asks if Ekattor reported something wrong: Aminur Rahman Sajib to the national team, when he barely played or scored this season, instead of Rony, Sabuj or defender Wali Faisal.
Bangladesh vs Nepal: Mannaf vs Bimal, Ibrahim vs the Nepali defenders; let us make the Gorkhas our new prey, go for the kill Tigers.

Poster says Emily's last two goals were gift-like tap-ins, while his positioning, stamina, target-man sense, passing and ball control are horribly bad; he misses chance after chance yet is called the best forward and automatic choice, and there is a syndicate among national team players.
Rising star Faysal: goalkeeper Faysal Ahmed was key to Bangladesh's SAFF U16 title with two tiebreaker saves, and as an Airtel Rising Stars 2012 winner he got training at Manchester United.

Poster says he was attacked for wanting Bangoura in the national team, when everyone became patriots; with syndicate and packet anyone can do anything, and God knows what talent the coach looks for when bench-warmers are multi-talented to him.
Fan asks who will play for Bangladesh in the Sheikh Kamal Cup, saying not to guess but only answer if sure.
BPL matches should be given to Tangail district stadium because there are plenty of spectators there.

Poster has been roaming for three days to film a video of Sheikh Jamal Stadium in Faridpur, which is in better condition than Sylhet Stadium but has no floodlights; crowds are huge, yet Sheikh Jamal making it a home ground is stuck, and BFF should notice.
If BPL matches are telecast, popularity will grow a lot; Kolkata football became popular because Jalsha Movies telecast it.
Rabbi's defence-splitting pass, Rohit goal.
Started watching the match at 1-1; can call it a new start.
The match went well; hope victory comes.

Bangladesh's defence looks solid, with Salahuddin and Tutul stopping Bimal; only Rohit scored despite attacks from Ibrahim, Rabbi and Rohit; the strategy looks like solid defence and counter, and U19 goalkeeper Anisul Islam looks like another Aminul-Biplob in the making.
Let's go Tigers.
One-word post: 'Ofs' (offsides, during the match).
Poster says on turf a fast short shot can fool the goalkeeper, the way they run.
Our goalkeeper is awesome.
Mannaf does not understand Ibrahim's pass and Ibrahim does not understand Mannaf's; individual skill, dribbling and speed are very good, but why so many wrong passes?
No problem, we will be champions, In Sha Allah.

Better team won today; well played Nepal, well deserved win; Badsha's mistake was unexpected, Ibrahim and Mannaf have a long way to go, and the typical defensive counter-attack Titu strategy struck again; good luck against India in the semi.
Sarcastic one-liner: but that is De Kruif's fault.
Lost the match due to Titu's rubbish tactics.
Bad luck for us; Badsha is not fully fit, and Rohit's goal was world class; best luck for the next match.
Almost everything was fine, just two rubbish goals conceded; no problem, a win is wanted next match, though the attack has lots of problems.

Poster is impressed by Bangladesh's play and hopes the U19s beat Nepal despite Titu's wrong tactics, as Sheikh Jamal won in Kyrgyzstan despite Afusi's negative formation; laments the injury-time set-piece own goal and asks why there is no psychologist; recalls the 1999 seniors beating India in the semi.

Poster tells fans to calm down: Bangladesh are in the semi-final, two more wins make them champions, and Rohit, Mannaf and Ibrahim will bloom; Bangladesh already hold the SAFF U16 and SA Games titles, and the SAFF U19 title is coming.

Ibrahim nutmegged a Nepali defender and hit the crossbar from near the left flank, a shot that would have been one of the year's best goals; Bangladesh dominated Nepal, especially in the second half, and nobody writes about Ibrahim.
Our U19 team is pretty good and should be trusted; nothing to be disappointed about in today's defeat, as the main aim is the AFC U19 championship and the SAFF U19 is just practice.

entities.name: Bangladesh Football - Walking Around The Dreams

posts.summary: Appeal to all group members to help grow the group by adding friends from their friendlists.
Poster says the team's performance impressed him, as Titu also said, and many are needlessly disappointed; links GoalNepal stories on Nepal's coach and supporters being disappointed.
Poster says apart from two or three online papers he cannot stand the rest, and was shocked by a priyo.com football report written by people with no football knowledge.
Priyo.com link about cricketers having fake IDs and footballers not; poster says he is not satisfied with Wahed brother.
Poster praises Zahid: he may be the badass of the team but he has the guts, and he made supporting the team worthwhile.
Poster quotes that besides Zahid on the wing there are Enamul Haque, Sohel Rana, Jewel Rana, Toklis and Komol, and notes Enamul on the wing with nothing more to say.

Fantasy commentary for 3 September: Mamunul's free kick is fisted away by Mathew Ryan, Jedinak's shot is intercepted by Jamal, Jamal passes to Zahid and GOAL, Bangladesh level 1-1 and silence the crowd.
After 2001, Bangladesh will again play a World Cup-playing giant: they lost 6-0 to Saudi Arabia in 2001 and face Australia on 3 September; a respectable loss will do.

Very long tribute to Enamul Haque: 18 goals in 24 matches this season as a centre-forward, 7 goals in 10 national team matches, SA Games 2010 hero, 5 goals in one league match, the 2005 AFC Cup winner against Nebitci Balkanabat, and a career hurt by injuries, BFF and club neglect; Muktijodha's Italian coach Flavio Raffo moved him back to striker.

Profile of Jewel Rana: a promising young forward from Jhenaidah whose father is a vegetable farmer, Mohammedan's best player, who tormented Tajikistan's defence and is the poster's bet against Australia; Sheikh Jamal have offered for him.
Poster asks who gets the money from stadium ticket sales.
Probable road to the 2016 AFC Cup group stage for Sheikh Jamal: beat Turkmenistan with a better margin than the AFG2 vs PAK1 winner and face Al Hidd of Bahrain, otherwise Fanja SC of Oman, both away.
Bangladesh's SAFF U19 semi-final opponents are India U19; poster hopes the U19s repeat the U16s' performance against India.

Confident Mamunul is not afraid of Australia: ranked 61st against Bangladesh's 170th, captain Mamunul says they are not afraid and will play the match of their lives in Perth on 3 September, while De Kruif says 85 percent of the tactics will be defensive.
SAFF U19 semi-final: Bangladesh face India after India beat Maldives 3-0 to top Group B and Bangladesh lost to hosts Nepal on a last-minute own goal; the other semi is Afghanistan vs Nepal.
Poster recalls the 2011 SAFF Games loss to Nepal from a last-minute 50-yard free kick, and says three ghosts haunt Bangladesh football: the Nepal ghost, the last-minute ghost and the set-piece ghost.
Credits - Ethar bro.
Fan asks what time the SAFF U19 semi-final, Bangladesh vs India, is.
Joke: Ronaldo scoring a penalty is called Penaldo, Messi scoring one is Pessi, so what is boss Emily called when he scores a penalty? Pemisi.
Fan asks if this is Malaysia's national team, a full-strength side, and whether it is FIFA-recognised.
Emily is being talked about a lot in the Facebook football neighbourhood; France Emily will give the fitting reply on the field, In Sha Allah.
Poster thinks Bangladesh should surprise Australia with all-out attack.
Spam post advertising an autolike website (fblikesfree250.wapka.mobi).
What if Bangladesh play all defence against Australia and score the winning goal from a penalty in the 89th minute to make history?
Garbled post about Malaysia's defence (Kelantan, Amirul Tajuddin) facing Bangladesh on Saturday.
Good news: the poster got a mail from Buriram FC Thailand.
Poster urgently asks for photos of goalkeeper Ashraful Islam Rana and defender Nasirul Islam Nasir.
A moment of Mamunul bhai's practice at the Sheikh Jamal ground before going to Australia.

Long post: the poster always imagined playing for Bangladesh against Australia, Uzbekistan, Japan, Qatar and Iran, and De Kruif's compact-defence and quick-transition tactics match that dream; recalls Malaysia vs Japan 2012, Thailand vs Australia 2014 and Bangladesh's 2006 qualifiers, hoping the players respond to the tactics.
Defender Mohammad Atiquzzaman, winger Sad Uddin and defender Khalil Bhuiyan have been excluded from the Bangladesh squad for the AFC U16 Championship.
The Bangladesh national team left the country to play Malaysia and Australia; best of luck, Bangladesh.

Poster asks what Bangladesh's tactics against Australia could be: defence plus counter-attack, a 1-9-0 with Sohel and Jewel's speed on the wings; the only problem is no good forward, and he wants the fight seen in the first half against Kyrgyzstan.
'Nothing to say', with a Facebook story link.

entities.name: Sailor BFF U15 National Football Championship

posts.summary: Sailor U15 final round: Feni beat Sylhet 3-1 at Bangabandhu Stadium (Ali, Shamrul, Tamim), and Natore beat Barisal 2-1 at the Abahani ground (Asaduzzaman, Saklain; Arif).

entities.name: United Arab Emirates national football team

posts.summary: The SAFF U16 champions face Asia: AFC U16 qualifiers start 16 September in Dhaka against Saudi Arabia and UAE, and BFF announced the 27-member squad.
Video of Kamalapur Stadium's current look, filmed from the poster's rooftop after a group member asked for it.
Prediction: Bangladesh U19 2, India U19 1; let us see.
Fan asks for a live link to watch the Bangladesh vs India match.
Poster left his PC to follow the match; the red-green jersey feels out of this world, and victory will come, In Sha Allah.
Nepali spectators are supporting Bangladesh against India, as expected.
Poster asks how old India's No. 11 is, guessing at least 23.
Poster says horrible football happened, with no organised attack.
Rohit cannot be found on the field; he is tightly marked.
Spam post advertising an autolike website (manvs.cf) for Facebook statuses and photos.
Poster says the referee keeps supporting India.
Sarcastic praise: congratulations Titu, you have won our hearts, the trophy can come later; brace for 'Titu is God' posts.
No one controls luck; many good players miss penalties, India got referee benefit with a retaken penalty and their players are older too; well played boys, better things lie ahead.
Poster asks what is happening that India reach or win the final every time.
Sarcastic post: in the football wave, Titu's tactics screwed football, and Bangladesh is looking for him in the dugout against Australia.
Abusive post: the poster says he could coach better than Titu, at least with a positive mentality, and that syndicate-packed people cannot develop football.

Poster says Titu hurried to get Bangladesh beaten by Malaysia before the Australia match, switching between 4-1-4-1 and 5-4-1; a man who fields five defenders against Sri Lanka cannot be expected to do more.

Mock breaking news: Mourinho, Van Gaal, Luis Enrique and Guardiola are in a tug of war to appoint Titu as assistant after his heroic sideline performance, and Argentina wants him as head coach to bring a World Cup.
Poster defends Titu against the Indian Football Live page, calling it nonsense to say Titu played defensively.
If Titu stays for the AFC qualifiers, Bangladesh will finish third in the group; the U19 squad has plenty of good players, but how can they win if five defend from the start?
Poster blames Titu's reckless tactics for the loss and says Maruful Haque should be given a chance.

Poster says he never liked Saiful Bari Titu as a coach, a lifelong believer in defensive tactics, and asks why Bangladesh played so defensively against India when attacking would have won; BFF knows no coach besides Titu.

Poster defends Titu: everyone is abusing him, but losing on tiebreakers is not his fault; India's players were over-aged and the tournament was strong, Titu's plan succeeded but players missed passes and penalties under tension.

Poster defends the 5-3-2: what matters is the result, the defence line was doubtful so three stoppers against India were obligatory, and the team never trained a full day together before the tournament.
Failure is the key to success; no use regretting now, the question is how to move forward.
Mocking post: Mohammedan's Super Cup win and Saiful Bari Titu's emergence in Bengal's sky, the rest is history of clouds, rain and tears.

Fantasy coaching staff for the 2022 World Cup: head coach Maruf, assistant Gilani, a Dutch trainer, a German goalkeeper coach and a German/English conditioning coach; poster calls himself a virtual pundit.
An England 3rd division club will play in the Sheikh Kamal Cup, coming through Afusi.
Short post: sweet revenge.
Poster saw a notification that Saiful Bari Titu posted in the group, searched for it, could not find it, then saw the notification actually said Saiful Islam Jitu posted.
Poster urges Bangladesh football fans to scold local channels so they wake up and at least telecast the Australia vs Bangladesh match live.
Poster says he never thought a coach could take a defensive strategy with three good strikers in the team, none of whom are unfit or lord-like, and the opponents are not miles ahead either.
Poster asks what kind of formation 5-3-2 is, long ball or counter-attack, challenging those defending Titu to answer.
Poster asks fans to stop blaming Titu for the defeat and be patient: it was only a practice tournament, and they should see what Titu does in September before judging.
Post about pressing the reality button, with what the poster feels Bangladesh vs Australia will be (likely a meme/score prediction).
Fan asks for the Facebook IDs of some national team players, ex and present, and of coaches.
Daily Star quote: 'We feel for this U-19 team not because they have lost but for not being allowed to play their natural game'; poster asks if everyone agrees.
Two clubs are interested in Rizwan Ahmed; poster asks if fans are excited to see him in the Bangladesh league.
Reasat married a Bangladeshi girl and may be looking to settle here; if he finds a club and keeps his head right, he can make his way back to the top.

BFF started a football academy at Sylhet BKSP and FIFA will provide artificial turf if BFF owns the ground for 20 years; the National Sports Council agreed to extend the lease from 5 to 20 years, so the turf will be laid soon.

Long praise of Maruful Haque, who benched Emily on form and won the treble with Sheikh Russel, attacked Busan IPark despite going 2-0 down, and was the first to protest fixed matches in the media, for which BFF banned him instead of investigating; also praises Mohammedan coach Joshi for trusting youngsters.
Poster asks fans not to blame coaches for every loss, as they are human too, or no coach will want to coach Bangladesh in the future.

Defence of coach Titu against trolling: he is defensive by design, score then defend, and the 5-3-2 formation is the same tactic Van Gaal, Dunga and Mourinho use, so it is logic for them but foolishness for Titu; that is why ex-players do not coach here.
Poster asks everyone: if you got to see Titu face to face, what would you do?
UK soccer league wants to buy the whole BPL from BFF; poster asks if BFF will accept.
Fan asks when the match is, 4:45 or 6:45.
Fan asks for the assist list in the Bangladesh Premier League 2014-15.
Video of an excellent free kick taken by Jamal Bhuiyan (YouTube link).
Tomorrow is the Bangladesh-Malaysia football battle.
Poster picks a best XI (defence Meshu, Munna, Raihan; midfield Mamunul, Jamal, Vincent, Emon; forwards Zahid, Jewel, Sohel, Emily) and hopes for victory tomorrow.

Poster heard foreign footballers got citizenship after five years in the league to strengthen the national team on the coach's advice, but wonders where they are and is disappointed not to see them in the Australia squad.
Fan asks what Chittagong Abahani's position is.
After a UK 3rd division club, Afghan club Shaheen Asmayee FC has agreed to play the Sheikh Kamal international tournament; Chittagong Abahani plan to contact New Radiant, Nepal MNC and Ratnam SC.
Poster says almost certainly no channel will show tomorrow's match and pleads that someone show the Australia one, so the dreamers can at least see something.
'History in making' with a GoalBangladesh Facebook photo link.
Fan asks who Ashhab 1323 is, the person who edits the Bangladesh national team's Wikipedia page.
FIFA friendly preview: Bangladesh vs Malaysia, with a link.

The next 10 days are a turning point for Bangladesh football: a friendly vs Malaysia today, then the Australia away qualifier on 3 September and Jordan in Dhaka; if Mamunul and co. play well, good things await the fans.
Fan asks if there is live streaming of today's match and to share it if so.

entities.name: United Arab Emirates national football team

posts.summary: Newspaper preview: 'confidence-less' Malaysia, bottom of World Cup qualifying Group A with 1 point after a 6-0 loss to Palestine, treat today's friendly as a lab to regain confidence; coach Dollah Salleh is wary of Bangladesh and may field Bangabandhu Cup U23 winners.
Fan asks which channel will show today's match, the match time (7:15?), whether it is FIFA-recognised, and notes no update on Forza Football.
Nepal are the first champions of the SAFF U19 Championship; congratulations.
Fan asks for match news, whether kickoff has happened, and why there is no match thread or update status.
Fan asks for a match update.

Poster wonders when he will see Zahid play again, though the Jewel-Sohel pair is playing well and Jamal Bhuiyan, man of the tournament in the last three tournaments, is on fire; asks if Emily is a false nine.
Fan asks for the scoreline and any live commentary link.
Half time in Bangladesh vs Malaysia.

Half time: Bangladesh 0-0 Malaysia; Sohel's brilliant saves in the first half, Mamun, Hemanta, Jamal and Jewel excellent in midfield, but Sohel Rana is nowhere to be found; hopes second-half changes bring the goal.
Fan asks who is playing well.
Goalkeeper Shahidul Alam Sohel alone is stopping Malaysia.
Poster asks why the coach is not bringing Zahid on.
Poster says Bangladesh are playing rubbish.
Enamul is coming on and Bangladesh supporters are cheering for him.
One-word post: red card (during the match).
Fan asks if the match is showing on any channel.
Shots on target: Bangladesh 1, Malaysia 13; all hail the defence.
Full time: Bangladesh 0-0 Malaysia; well played Bengal Tigers, best player goalkeeper Sohel; now mission Australia.
Bangladesh drew the match and Shahidul was tremendous: BAN 0 - MAS 0.
Well played Bangladesh, 0-0 with Malaysia; fans are with the team under the red-green flag.
A match of Malaysia vs Shahidul Alam; poster did not get what the others did.

Poster read GoalBangladesh commentary: the defence stood led by Sohel, the benefit of three months with a Sheikh Jamal goalkeeper coach; but questions why Sohel stayed till the 76th minute and Emily always plays, hinting at a syndicate, and demands a full-time coaching team.
Today's hero is goalkeeper Shahidul Alam Sohel; without his saves the result would have been different, and now mission Australia, for which he has readied himself.
Shahidul 10/10: poster describes his saves against Malaysia, including a sprint to stop Ridwan with an empty goal, and 15 on-target saves, saying he did not miss Aminul for the first time in ages.
Poster says the benefit of a goalkeeping coach is slowly showing, and hopes BFF also gives weight to a fitness coach.

Bangladesh drew the friendly with Malaysia; the biggest contribution was goalkeeper Shahidul Alam stopping attack after attack in the 0-0 draw at Shah Alam Stadium, ahead of the Australia qualifier on 3 September.
Teasing post: where are the fans of Emily?
Post (likely a photo) noting that the crowd scenes seen in Bangladeshi tea stalls are now how Malaysia is watching the Bangladesh vs Malaysia match.

Judging the national team's situation, not much can be expected; BFF must upgrade the league, which they started by signing with the UK soccer league; a draw against quality Malaysia, whose players play in the AFC Cup, is good.
Poster says now everyone will start trolling Emily instead of coach Titu; 2 of Bangladesh's last 4 goals are Emily's, and there will be haters.
An away draw is not bad at all.

Poster laments he could not watch the drawn match for lack of data; Bangladesh could easily have a sports channel, with Hamim Group, Beximco/Papon and Gazi Group all having the money, but will and love for football are lacking.
Well played boys today, keep roaring.

Poster says De Kruif was dissatisfied with the squad and wanted young players, but a syndicate stopped him dropping anyone and BFF blocked stopping the league for World Cup preparation; with full freedom he would have taken the team to another level.
Bangladesh vs Australia will be shown live on Fox Sports 3, and any Bangladeshi channel can buy it from them.
Video of Sunday Chizoba, the Blue Brigade's grenade, striker in the 2014-15 season (YouTube link).
From a few posts the poster gathers Bangladesh played horribly with 10 men, the goalkeeper was brilliant and the match was drawn; whatever, just need to win against Australia.

Poster says if Bangladesh had attacked with full effort today and then flown to Australia, fatigue would have meant a 10-0 loss; Malaysia will lose in Bangladesh someday, and he senses something big against the Aussies.
A minute's silence for those who said football in Bangladesh is dead; fans still love it whether inside or outside Bangladesh.

Long rant: Fox Sports 3 will show Bangladesh vs Australia and local channels could buy it, but Channel i buys Brazil/Argentina friendlies and talks big while ignoring Bangladesh vs Malaysia and the Australia qualifier; channels care only about business, not social responsibility.
Fan asks for Shahidul Yousuf's year-to-year club career and Jewel Rana's total league goals this season.

After Aminul and Biplob, another tireless sentry: Sohel!

posts.summary: Worried about the pitch: at BNS on 8 September there will be the World Cup qualifying match against Jordan, again in the same month on the 16th and 18th there are two AFC Under-16 matches, and again on this ground from 2 October there will be the AFC Under-19 tournament; in that stadium now the Sailor BFF Under-15 tournament is going on, the 2nd semi-final was on a muddy pitch, can the final be held, with today's rain, can the pitch be fixed in these few days, or will we have to play on a muddy pitch?

We have no money, so we have kept a part-time coach; but what is the news of our coach, as his profile and record are all more or less good, why does he not get a job, and staying as a part-time coach like this is not very good for his reputation either.

De Kruif and Rene Koster, after becoming coaches of the Bangladesh football team, took an extraordinary initiative, as this Dutchman started efforts to bring Bangladeshi-origin footballers staying abroad into the national team by giving them Bangladeshi citizenship; the main objective, though, was to end the striker crisis, but at the start Bangladesh got a holding midfielder, Jamal Bhuiyan, who played in FC Copenhagen's youth team and surprised everyone from the start, with what ball holding, tackling, taking possession of the ball or distribution, as in everything the boy is extraordinary, and not only that, the boy is completely different from ten other Bangladeshi footballers, every day sweating in the gym, stretching and terrible hard work, and Jamal is like a reflection of a European footballer; before Jamal came, most footballers objected to Jamal's inclusion in the team, but Jamal cemented his place in the team by his own merit, and not only that, in someone's opinion Jamal is South Asia's best holding midfielder, in someone's opinion Asia's, and Jamal Bhuiyan is not called Asia's Xabi Alonso for nothing; Mamunul is another pillar of the midfield, with picture-like passes and eye-catching football as the big strength of the Bangladesh captain, and not only supplying the ball to the attack, the main responsibility of the attack is also on this Chittagong boy's shoulders; Hemanta Vincent Biswas's rise is like a fairy tale, as this stylish midfielder who came up from school football has been called for trials by several European clubs more than once, and polished at BKSP and Mohammedan, this free-kick specialist has become one of the team's most important members in a very short time; before facing the toughest test in their history, the midfield's skill is much more hopeful, and to come out well in the test, there is no alternative to keeping possession of the ball, as the nature of this match depends on this trinity of Jamal, Mamunul and Hemanta, and this match therefore gives hope and shows dreams, or it can be said, the three princes of the midfield force us to see hopeful dreams.

Bangladesh-Australia: Australia in 'trouble' before the match, as before the World Cup qualifying match against Bangladesh, the Australia football team is going through a 'problem', with injuries to the team's important players a big problem, and due to injury, coach Ange Postecoglou is not getting several important players for the Bangladesh match, that is old news, but the thing that has become a headache for Australian football 72 hours before the match is the player-federation conflict, and because of this conflict, Tim Cahill and co. are boycotting all formalities with sponsors, as the conflict between the Professional Footballers Australia, the organisation of Australia's professional footballers, and Football Federation Australia over money is now at its peak, after a collective bargaining agreement expired, according to ABC Online; because of this conflict, the PFA says there will be no problem in Thursday's World Cup qualifying match against Bangladesh, but they have announced a boycott of all commercial activities of the football federation outside the match, and as part of this, a promotional event to be held on Tuesday at a shopping mall in Perth has been announced postponed, and Australia's professional footballers feel that after the expiry of the collective bargaining agreement, the federation, by not taking new initiative in this regard, is snatching the players' rights, and apologising to Australian football fans in this regard, the players said they had nothing else to do in this regard.

Without beating around the bush, let me come directly to the work: our football has become Dhaka-centric, because teams relegated from the BPL go down to the Championship League, and from the Championship League to the Dhaka League Division, a strange thing, because of which the teams have become Dhaka-centric, as Dhaka's teams rise to the Championship League and Dhaka's teams get relegated; we need an intermediary tournament, which will be between the Championship League and the district first division league, with the district first division league champion teams playing in that tournament, 64 teams, can you imagine, as football will be on the field all year and football will be all over the country, and from 64 teams, 3 teams will go to the Championship League, while three teams will be relegated from the Championship League, and besides, there are many teams, that is, Dhaka-based teams, which will also play this tournament, and from here they will be relegated to the Dhaka First Division; the home venue of the district champion teams will be the district stadiums, and matches will be played in a leg system, so this way the teams will get home advantage, and on this pretext the stadiums will be developed, the DFAs will be active, and as a result, there will be no cheating, and it will be seen that maybe football will regain its lost glory; we will not say football's golden past, we will say golden present, and this generation wants that, the generation wants to see football's golden present, by Hasan Tasin.
Initial decision to sack Kruif; he did not want to coach the team in Australia demanding arrears, according to Ekattor TV.
Lodewijk de Kruif did not agree to conduct practice demanding the owed money; after arranging payment of 70%, Kruif was finally persuaded; BFF has initially decided to sack Kruif; source: Ekattor TV.
Brother, Bhutan was at the very bottom of the FIFA ranking just a few months ago, now the poster sees 164, which is ahead of Bangladesh too; what happened, the poster doesn't understand anything.

'If you do not show your ability than it's a waste of your talent': after whitewashing the Pakistanis, Tamim said this quote, and the poster thinks because of this attitude of playing fearlessly, Bangladesh could play so well; now come to the real topic, how much is the possibility of getting a point against the Aussies, as at home against a comparatively weak team they played well but could earn only 1 point, so there, how realistic is it to play for a point from Australia's soil, and even if we play ultra-defensively, can we keep a clean sheet, and rather, should we not forget who the opponent is and play our natural game and show our talent, as 4-0 to 5-2, 6-3 score lines feel better, and maybe with this match's performance, our Jewel got a call from a European team, or a goal on such a big stage will inspire his whole career.
Well, what are the names of the 2 Bangladeshi-origin players who have come from Wales to the BD football team? Please let me know.

Dear Kruif, you are the best coach of Bangladesh I have seen; come, in what respect are you the best coach: for 3 consecutive years you were the national team's coach, in between you left 1-2 times and came back again, and later you became a picnic-mode coach, and before this, no coach could stay more than 6 months, so in this respect you have achieved a very big thing; in the next match you will not be able to stand in the dug-out against Australia, so do one thing, go home, you are sick anyway, and in the next match, Titu bhai will be Bangladesh's head coach; anyway, we will get something good in the match.
So, it's just one day to go, just one day to go.

Come, let us prepare to bid farewell to our best coach De Kruif, and keep remembering the gifts he gave; a 3-year relationship cannot be severed like this, and tomorrow the poster will upload a photo of him.

Before judging whether Kruif is good or bad, we need to keep 3 things in mind: first, could we use him for work; second, even if we used him, could we give him freedom in his work; third, could we give him the respect he deserved; the poster admits he did not do the work properly this time, but what is the guarantee that BFF would have given the money after coming back from Australia, as they did not do little dilly-dallying.
Australia is a bigger pauper than us: Australia's players have called for a boycott of the match because they did not get money; with salary troubles on both sides, will the match happen in the end?

As ordinary people, the poster did not like Kruif as a coach, but since BFF did not give him a proper environment to work, he gave him the benefit of doubt; what happened yesterday, BFF is more at fault than Kruif; dear BFF, if you do this, no coach will come and stay, cut your coat according to your cloth, and if you cannot keep a coach, do not unnecessarily ruin your reputation for show, and you have poured money anyway when no work was done, and you have no right to waste the country's money this way; in three years you paid money, earned a bad name, and gained nothing; if you cannot, make Maruf bhai the coach, take only Coleman, and let the goalkeeper coach stay, and don't keep them part-time, not with other clubs, keep them with the academy, as after a few days, the trouble over salary with the coach is not good, and it is embarrassing, which again some people do not have.

Live streaming link for the Australia vs Bangladesh match; not sure whether it will work, as someone gave it in the page's message, but anyway save it, wherever you see ash, blow it and see, you may find a priceless jewel.

Dream commentary: Jahid is going faster with the ball, the speedy cheetah is looking so confident, oh God, dribbling dribbling dribbling is everywhere, ZH7 dribbled 5 Australian defenders like a magician, Socceroos defenders felt like ZH7 is total invisible, Zahid passes the ball to Mamunul from the right wing, shot, but the Australian goalkeeper saved the ball like a flying spider, unbelievable, Bangladeshi supporters are about to cry, oh wait, General Enamul Haque is there, he got the ball, Enamul nutmegs Tim Cahill, bullet shot to the goal post, gooooal, 94 minutes Bangladesh 1-0 Australia, it's raining in Perth today, otherwise everyone could see the emotional tears in Enamul, Mamun, Jahid, Jamal and Hemonto's eyes, wipe off tears champions, wipe off; by the way, it is just 19 hours to go here in the Planet Earth, big match Bangladesh vs Australia, 3 September, 5 pm BDT.

Australia vs Bangladesh: in football, these two countries will face each other for the first time tomorrow; the matter is quite like a dream, and the result may be like a nightmare, but whatever the result, the poster hopes the Bangladesh footballers will learn a lot from this match; many regretted that Bangladesh is in a group with Australia, but to the poster this seems a big gain for Bangladesh, as even if Bangladesh concedes 7 or 8 goals, they will learn something, and at least they will understand reality; many say the friendship between India and Nepal is a bit too much, as if needed they play more matches among themselves, and just like that, we also got a friend country, its name is Sri Lanka, and we also invited them for any need and lost matches, but there was not much benefit there, and the poster hopes there will be benefit this time, as even losing to a world class team, a lot can be learned; by one calculation, Bangladesh should have fallen in an even tougher group, because BFF will not arrange a match of Bangladesh with Brazil or Argentina, they will arrange a match of a team like Brazil or Argentina vs Australia at this Dhaka ground; anyway, in this Australia vs Bangladesh match, may Bangladesh not lose before losing, and best wishes for the team.

Everyone the poster sees has started dreaming in their sleep about our football, look, look, it's fun; anyway, at one time the poster also used to dream, and now with study time he is under pressure, still he can't stop reading your statuses, so dream and write in status, sleeping or awake.
In the world of thought, everything is possible; like this moment the poster is imagining Bangladesh will take the lead against Australia with Hemanta Vincent's goal; ah, what a sweet dream.
Bare Kaler Kantho article link.

Elite coach coaching: BFF has brought a coach from FIFA to coach a total of 30 coaches selected from the whole country, which felt very good, as almost all the good coaches of the country are there, like Jilani bhai, Manik bhai and Maruful Haque bhai and many others, and everyone is very happy; the FIFA coach says our coaches are mostly all good, but have little idea about modern football, which the poster says they already said long ago; source: Ekattor News.
Whatever anyone says, if Kruif did not conduct practice, BFF is responsible for that, because bringing an expensive coach and not paying the salary has become a profession of BFF.
Mushfiqur Rahim posted on his page wishing the football team, very good, but most people's comments are when is the match and at what time.

Kruif did not agree to conduct practice over salary money, and later he went to practice after taking 5 thousand euros, right? But BFF sacked him, is that after the Australia match or after the Jordan match? Meanwhile, the Australia team's footballers have reportedly started trouble over salary, somewhere the poster sees they are boycotting activities other than the match, and somewhere he sees they have threatened to boycott the match too; brother, what is the actual event, as after reading chemistry his head was already tingling and seeing all this it is completely spinning.

Socceroos, in case you missed it: listen to the Socceroos v Bangladesh pre-match press conference below to hear our Tim Cahill named as captain for tomorrow night, as well as a whole lot more, with a link.
Who knows what happened between BFF and Kruif, but Kruif's direct statement has been found, with a link.

GoalBangladesh: 'Coach, we heard about a rumour that you have been sacked?'; Bangladesh coach: 'Really, that's a surprise for me, I didn't know that'; GoalBangladesh: last night, one TV channel spread the news about a salary dispute; Bangladesh coach: 'There are good journalists as well as bad; we need to learn better journalism, still we are very poor in this arena; the only person who can sack me is BFF boss Salahuddin, and I have a very good rapport with him'; the poster calls it drunk media and their shitty report.
Bro, I heard Channel 9 will live telecast the BD vs AUS match?

Before the match against Australia, BFF took a revolutionary step: the decision was to grant citizenship to a few African footballers playing regularly in Bangladesh and include them in the national team; the idea was undoubtedly timely, as for many years our striker crisis has been at its peak, but due to opposition from many former and current players and considering the foreigners' ages, BFF cancelled this project; the biggest weakness of our football team is scoring, with lack of physical ability and the domestic teams' dependence on foreign strikers as the big reasons; Emily has aged and form has not been there for a long time, and Emily, who never missed a penalty in life, missed one six months ago, and if the poster talks about Enamul, Enamul had been lost, but this league's comeback of this stylish born striker can be called royal, though the problem is in that one place, whims; since we will play only one striker, whichever one will play in the eleven, and now whether Emily or Enamul starts is entirely the coach's decision; the two wings are somewhat stable, as against Malaysia, Jewel Rana and Sohel Rana started, and against Australia probably they will, but there is no place to deny that Zahid Hossain, our super seven, is the team's best winger, though he himself is somewhat responsible for the collapse of his career, yet Zahid in form is dangerous for any opponent; one day before the ball rolls in Perth, it must be admitted that compared to other parts of the team, the attack's position is quite fragile, as football is a game of goals, and even if you want to draw minimally, you have to go on the attack, but there is only one hopeful thing: if Emily and Enamul can squeeze themselves, there is no harm in seeing sweet dreams.
Apparently Channel 9 will show the match.
Tim Cahill: 'We know Bangladesh are good on the counter attack as we saw when they played Malaysia'; on the counter attack, Emily bhai's speed is like a racing car.
Post consisting only of a smiling emoticon.

Mamunul: Yes, I also see it that way; if we play well, calls to play somewhere or other may come for us, so the match has come with a different significance than ten other international matches, and I will want to present myself by playing very good football.

On 30 August at 6.30 pm, the poster sat down to watch Khelajog on Ekattor TV; he could not watch the match against Malaysia, nor did he get a match report, as Khelajog started by showing match reports of the EPL, La Liga and German League, then a break, and returning from the break, they just said verbally that Bangladesh drew, with no match report; Bangladesh will play against Australia, no one has the ability to show the match, yet they are making a fake news and happily broadcasting it; it is better not to have such media than to have it, and the poster spits on their faces.

Very good news: the CEO of GoalBangladesh.com has had a successful meeting with Fox Sports and FFA, the Federation of Football Australia, and you can watch the game tomorrow through a live streaming link; get ready.
When will the Bangladesh-Australia match start tomorrow? Will any channel show it?
Can 2005 come tomorrow in a slightly different way? The place is the same, the dream is the same.
And only twenty-four hours left.
Wherever we go, we represent Bangladesh, so we should remember not to let the country's honour be lost.
Some slum boys are making the group's environment worse day by day, posting such bad pictures, and the poster's head gets angry.
The poster hopes tomorrow the players will present their best game, as this is the biggest opportunity to prove themselves.

Play attacking, play fearless; the poster's idea is they are thinking we will play defensively tomorrow, but if we attack them at the start and shock them, it will be great, and by playing defensively we have never got results; and on the two wings the poster wants to see Jewel and Zahid, as the skill and speed of the two seem more effective to him than Sohel's.
Which channel will show tomorrow's Bangladesh vs Australia match live? If anyone knows, please tell.

Year 2067, Bangabandhu Stadium: in the Gold Cup league final, Bangladesh vs Spain face each other, as last time Bangladesh were knocked out by Spain in the World Cup semi, and today is the turn for revenge; in front of 95 thousand people, the greatest techniques of football begin, with Spain scoring first from a corner with a zero-degree shot, then Bangladesh conceding another goal playing too high up, and at the end of 45 minutes Sabbir scores a goal for Bangladesh with a shot from midfield, making it Bangladesh 1, Spain 2 at half time; in the second half Bangladesh starts playing rhythmically again, but with a beautiful bicycle shot by Basilis, Spain goes another goal ahead, then Bangladesh increases the sharpness of attack and at 70 minutes reduces the gap with a header from a corner, making it Bangladesh 2, Spain 3, and unbelievably, Spain's defender Beniham gives a wrong pass and Jonny, getting the goalkeeper alone, puts the ball in the net, levelling the two teams at three-three at 72 minutes; Spain reduces defender positions and starts attacking play, and in attack and counter-attack, even in the air-conditioned Bangabandhu Stadium, 95 thousand people start sweating, and when everyone is disappointed, then Sabbir, who is Real's right winger, scores with a diagonal shot from almost 55 metres away at 92.35 minutes, a wave of excitement rising in the whole gallery, with Spain's players kneeling down and Bangladesh's players running to the dug-out towards the coach, where old coach Mamunul is standing and crying, as many years ago he also cried and today he is crying too; ah, the dream broke, the clock is 3 am, and it seems sleep will not come tonight, so the poster shared it.

Prothom Alo article, 'Kahiler o to duti hat, duti pa': FIFA ranking, achievements, quality of play and star footballers, the distance between Australia and Bangladesh is like an ocean, as a team that has played the World Cup four times and the current Asian champions cannot be bridged overnight, yet football is such a game that anything can happen in a fraction of a second, and Bangladesh captain Mamunul Islam says the match is thrilling, not frightening, promising his team will fight with all its might; in ranking, Australia is at 61 and Bangladesh at 170, yet Mamunul is not at all afraid of the Socceroos, saying Cahill is not someone from another planet, as he also has two hands and two legs, and though he may be a better player, they will each pour their best; coach Lodewijk de Kruif also accepts the gap between the two teams, but says his disciples will take the field against Australia fully prepared, as of course they are Asia's number one team, a wonderful team with a lot of experience and great players playing in Europe, and though they will take the field as underdogs, they have their own strategy and have analysed the opponent well; the Dutch coach reminded of football's proverb that anything can happen, noting he saw their last match against Kyrgyzstan, which Australia won 2-1, and Kyrgyzstan made the match difficult for Australia, and his players are not at all afraid, though they are respecting, but no one has come here to roam as a tourist.

Sad? Thinking why big teams dominate so much? Then I will not play you in your position, you will play in the place of the country's best winger; okay, still you will not play? Why? The poster does not want to comment on what Joarder said about the team's seniors in this Prothom Alo feature, as it is a much older incident and it is over, and here he copy-pasted the feature: Mamun Joarder, one of the last representatives of the golden time of Bangladesh football, said goodbye to football 13 years ago, and in August 2000 his tearful farewell from Dhaka's field made football lovers cry; after representing the country for seven consecutive years, he took farewell with pain and the suffering of not being able to give the country a big success in football, and that pain chases him even now; Mamun is now a Canada expatriate who regularly keeps track of the country's football, and going to watch an Abahani match at Bangabandhu Stadium with his wife and children, he was greatly disappointed, as the spectators could be counted on fingers, and in his opinion the popularity of the country's football is not even at the position of 10-12 years ago; he blames football organisers and clubs, and even former players, equally for the current state, as the terrible lack of professionalism in his time brought football to this place, and the black influence of politics in football has been the cause of ruin, saying politics has finished our football, and he has seen political interference in national team selection, with coaches like lame Jagannaths performing only nominal duties while the team was made in the upper levels, with an abundance of players from the ruling party's favourite club in the national team; he tells stories from 1993, when four goalkeepers had to be taken in the World Cup qualifiers squad in Japan-UAE only due to the tug-of-war between the country's two big clubs, and under pressure from the then ruling party, coach Kazi Salahuddin was bewildered, and an out-of-form goalkeeper was fielded against the then Asian champions Japan, with the national team losing 8-0 in Tokyo; in 1993 he was in great form, yet Salahuddin bhai could not field him, and Salahuddin bhai used to say, 'Mamun, this team is not mine, this is a team imposed from above'; he also saw the indiscipline of senior footballers in the so-called golden time, with seniors absent from the hotel all night before a match in Japan and entering the hotel swaying in the morning; in the 1992 league title-deciding match between Abahani and Mohammedan, word spread that he had a secret relationship with Mohammedan, and under pressure from officials, Salahuddin bhai did not keep him in the first XI, and in his place played Russian footballer Alexander Palinkov, but after Mohammedan went ahead 1-0, Salahuddin bhai fielded him, and he scored two goals within 15 minutes as Abahani won the title, the best match of his life; one of his biggest sorrows is getting an offer from a Malaysian professional league club in 1997 yet not being able to play, as Abahani's then officials did not give him permission and BFF also could not give him clearance due to Abahani's influence, and he blames club politics, noting that many in his time, Munna bhai, Rumi, Sabbir and Jewel Rana, got offers from leagues like Malaysia and Korea but could not play; playing under German coach Otto Pfister is the ultimate gift of his playing life, as Pfister liked him very much and a coach of his calibre will never come to Bangladesh again, yet they could not keep Pfister, who too was a victim of dirty politics in this country's football; in 1995, Bangladesh won the four-nation football title in Myanmar under Pfister, with Mamun scoring the winning goal in the 2-1 final win against Myanmar; and a word of Ulrich Schwab, coach of the Bangladesh team in the 1993 SAFF Games, still rings in his ears, that Schwab could not arrange the team as he wanted and, under political pressure, had to make Arif Hossain Moon captain despite keeping players like Monem Munna or Rumi in the team, and Moon sank the team by giving a wrong pass inside the box against Nepal, and Schwab later said that as long as there is politics in football in this country, Bangladesh will not be able to do anything, which Mamun now understands was correct; at this moment Mamun Joarder is living a peaceful, simple life in Canada, and football has given him everything, money, fame and glory, and he always wants to return something to football.

Fabio Lopez, born 17 June 1973, is an Italian football manager and former footballer, a coach with experience as youth coach of many Italian academy clubs and clubs affiliated to A.S. Roma, and many international experiences as a professional head coach; he was appointed head coach of FK Banga Gargždai in Lithuania in January 2007, his first team as a professional coach, and worked as scout for Atalanta and ACF Fiorentina, and in 2008 was instructor in a UEFA B course in the Lithuania Football Federation; he is a former goalkeeper whose playing career was cut short by a serious knee injury while with Agiatese in the 1992-93 season; after retiring he coached semi-professional and youth teams, won a Youth Cup in Umbria with a Roma affiliate team, became a scout of Fiorentina, obtained the youth coaches licence in 2000, and in 2007 obtained a UEFA A coaching licence, later a UEFA Pro licence; his coaching career includes Eurolimpia A.S. Roma Academy, Roma Team A.S. Roma Academy, FK Banga Gargždai, FK Siauliai, Sabah FA as technical director, PSMS Medan, where he saved the team from relegation, and B.G. Sports Club in the Maldives, where he took the team from zero points after four games to third place; managerial honours include regional cups with Eurolimpia and Roma Team, third place in the A Lyga with FK Siauliai, and third place with B.G. Sports Club, per Wikipedia.

New coach's bits and pieces: after bidding farewell to Dutch coach Lodewijk de Kruif, BFF has appointed Italy's Fabio Lopez in his place, initially for four months; born in 1973, this Italian's career profile is quite shiny, holding UEFA coaching licences A and B, with a coaching philosophy much like famous coach Fabio Capello's, preferring 4-4-2, 4-3-3 and 4-1-4-1; his playing career is not that rich, starting football at age six, joining AS Roma's youth team at around 12, then moving to a club named Agiatis as a goalkeeper, establishing himself as a top goalkeeper of Central Italy and playing regularly in Italy's Serie D, though the national team remained elusive; as a physical training specialist, Lopez has quite a name, and in his coaching career he has experience of several countries, spending an important time in Lithuania, as head coach of FC Siauliai in the A Lyga from 2008 to 2009, winning nine of 15 matches and finishing fourth, and as coach of FK Banga, losing only six of 27 matches and taking the weak team to the Lithuanian Cup quarter-finals; from 2012 to 2013 he was head coach of Maldives Premier League's Big Sports Club, and before that for one year head coach of Indonesian Premier League PSM Makassar, and in 2011 technical sports director of Malaysian club Sabah FA; an extra benefit of appointing Lopez for BFF may be that there will be no need to keep a new goalkeeping coach, because Lopez himself is a goalkeeping expert; how long Lopez will stay in Bangladesh, time will tell, but it can be assumed bringing him will cost BFF quite a lot, as wherever Lopez has coached he has taken good remuneration, and he was also the highest-paid coach in Maldives' history; source bdlive21.com.

U19 football: while the Australia cricket team has postponed coming to Bangladesh citing security reasons, the AFC U19 international football is sitting in Dhaka at exactly that time; in this competition starting tomorrow at Bangabandhu Stadium, host Bangladesh is with Uzbekistan, Bhutan, Sri Lanka; there is much talk about Bangladesh's security, and the US-UK have also told their citizens to be careful, but the foreign teams have not raised any question about this tournament in Dhaka, and they have not said anything about this to BFF either; a top official of the Sri Lanka team rather said, 'I don't see anything about Bangladesh's insecurity'; recently, the Bangabandhu Cup, the U16 AFC tournament and various international matches have happened in Dhaka without any trouble; in international competitions, there is usually a police van with the team, and this time too, that is staying, but this time, police security is also being given at the practice ground; BFF said that in the current situation, the security arrangements have been increased compared to before; the Bhutan team returned to Dhaka from BKSP yesterday, Uzbekistan came to Dhaka the day before yesterday, Sri Lanka this morning; all these teams' attention is around the ground performance; a top official of the Sri Lanka team said, 'We have come to play, so the game is the main consideration for us; we are not worried about security at all, and everything seems good here'; Sri Lanka recently played a tournament in China; like Bangladesh-Bhutan, this team is also considering Uzbekistan as the group best; in the unwritten fight for group runners-up, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Bhutan; among the ten groups, the best five runners-up will get a chance in the final round next year; the Bangladesh team wants to take this opportunity, and the whole team is committed to taking themselves one step up by reaching the final round; for this, wins against Sri Lanka and Bhutan are needed; head coach Saiful Bari thinks the win is possible; standing at the Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi ground yesterday, he said, 'We are ready to beat Sri Lanka and Bhutan'; that mission starts tomorrow itself with the Sri Lanka match.

Bangladesh coach Titu took the responsibility for failure: Bangladesh coach Saiful Bari Titu accepts the draw against Bhutan as failure, but in the reaction after the match, he did not walk the path of criticising his disciples; rather, he took all the responsibility for failure on his own shoulders; at the Bangabandhu Stadium on Sunday, in the 'A' group match of the AFC U19 Championship qualifiers, Bangladesh drew 1-1 due to the forwards' failure, and with this draw, Bangladesh's dream of playing in the main round in Bahrain in 2016 as one of the best five runners-up faded; Titu said, calling it a 'shameful matter' that they could not repeat beating Bhutan in the SAFF U19 Championship at home, 'We should have won against Bhutan at home; there was a chance to be the best runner-up in front of us, but we failed; a draw with Bhutan is not at all decent'; 'The full responsibility for failure is mine; Bhutan played pressing football; how they will play, how we have to play against them, all was told to the boys; my failure is that perhaps I could not make the boys understand, and I could not inspire them', Titu added; Bangladesh fell behind after conceding a goal in the sixth minute, and in the 77th minute, Masum Mia Jonny's goal brought the hosts back to level, but the whole match's wrong passes and Rohit-Rabbi-Nipu's confusion after entering the opposition's box surprised the coach; 'Why the boys didn't play in the first half as they played in the second half is a surprise to me; there is nothing more disappointing than this (this draw) in my coaching career'; compared to the first half, Bangladesh recovered a lot in the second half, but Titu said it was not enough to beat Bhutan, and he didn't forget to praise the opposition Bhutan's play; next Tuesday, Bangladesh will face Uzbekistan, who won two consecutive matches and are top of the group, and Titu accepts this as a match to keep alive the dream of the main round for the hosts in second place; he also said winning against favourite Uzbekistan is difficult; 'If we win the last match, we will also have a chance to go to the main round as group champions; if we draw, with five points, I think we have no chance of being the best runner-up; but besides something miraculous (beating Uzbekistan), we have to remember the reality too'; Bhutan's coach, who conceded seven goals to Uzbekistan in the first match, is not very happy with the result of the second match, and praising Bangladesh's attacking football in the second half, Choki Nima said, 'Better than us in all aspects; our goal was to give our best; I think we couldn't do that'; source: BD NEWS24.
BFF should back another coach in place of Saiful Bari Titu; there is enough doubt about his ability.

Coach Fabio Lopez on Mamunul and Rony's new positions: 'You see how Messi plays? He starts from the right side and goes inside when there is the ball; Mamunul did the same job today; Mamunul is the best player, so he must make sacrifice to play for the team', and 'Rony played in a new position because I see he has the potential of helping team playing in the middle', explained Lopez; 'I need to do some experiments because I don't have much time'; collected from The Daily Star.

Several national team footballers, unwilling to reveal their names, said, 'Where I will play, I cannot say; what the character will be, I don't know'; their statement: 'There is no problem in changing reality; the problem is in fundamental change'.

Mamunul himself is not willing to see himself like this; due to the change of place, he is inwardly angry and annoyed: 'I am trying to adapt to the new place, but to be honest, I am uncomfortable; I cannot play my best, so if my performance on the field is bad, no one can blame me, because the coach changed my position'.

The national team looks shaky; Lopez wants 'sacrifice' from Mamunul: he has played in one place for 10-12 years and is established today, but suddenly that place changes, and Bangladesh's football well-wishers may be shocked; Mamunul Islam means the craftsman who creates play in midfield, and as a playmaker, he not only spreads the ball both ways, he makes the ball for the striker like serving food on a plate, and the Bangladesh team's play has been revolving around Mamunul for several years, but in the Fabio Lopez era, there is an indication of a 'full stop' in this; the Italian coach has already tested Mamunul in striking once or twice, giving him a 'promotion', but he has used him more on the right side of midfield, and this is probably Mamunul's new position; yesterday's practice match between the national team and the BFF XI at BKSP gave that message, and there is no hint of good things in the message; rather, according to the footballers, the wind of ill omen is blowing; with Toklis kept on the left side of midfield, Mamunul was played on the right side, and with Emily not there, above was BJMC striker Nabib Newaz Jibon, and although the coach likes Nabib very much, he didn't seem amazing; actually, the eye stayed more on Mamunul, and although some spark was seen in his feet, the quality of playing the team and being a true leader was absent; Mamunul himself is not willing to see himself like this, and due to the change of place, he is inwardly angry and annoyed, 'I am trying to adapt to the new place, but to be honest, I am uncomfortable; I cannot play my best, so if my performance on the field is bad, no one can blame me, because the coach changed my position'; the coach surely has that right, and standing on the BKSP ground in the light and darkness, he reminded it, 'Look, Mamunul is the best player of this team; as Messi starts on the right and plays inside, Mamun did the same work today; I will want him to make a sacrifice for the team'; but Mamunul looks unhappy, and besides, the one he is playing in his place, Komol, is basically a winger, and in inside midfield is Shakhaowat Rony, whose main identity is as a striker; the most storm was on this Rony, as he had to go to defence to help, and he passed the ball in attack too, and standing outside the sideline, Lopez was heard shouting at least 50 times, 'Go Rony, go'; in an unfamiliar place, poor Rony was in a gasping state, 'I have never played in such an important place in midfield; both difficulty and problems are happening, but the coach wants it, what can I do'; Lopez explained his wish like this, 'Rony is playing in a new place; I am seeing how he can help the team from midfield'; there is a hidden undercurrent of anger in the team about this 'seeing' of the coach; winger Faisal Mahmud became a right-back that day, and from right-back, Raihan played as a stopper, yet stopper Rezaul is sitting; the four position changes in the first XI are the most eye-catching; the words of striker Emily, who was knocked out of the team with a tumour in his stomach, are memorable, 'It is better not to experiment so much in the team; before, doing these caused danger'; Mamunul also matched his voice with his friend yesterday, 'One or two experiments can happen in the team, but there is a fear of inviting danger in so many experiments'; Lopez also has arguments in favour of experiments, and since he didn't get time, he sees many more things to do in the team; his unprepared team beat the BFF XI 4-1, and in that team played Mobarak, Mintu Sheikh, Mamun Mia, Sabuz, Touhidul; the win is not big here, and what looks big is Lopez's experiments and the call for sacrifice from Mamunul.

A cautionary post: those who go to watch matches in the ground, you will see as soon as you enter, some people will come, who will want to sell match tickets for 5-10 taka less; avoid them, as the tickets are complimentary tickets, and tickets allotted in the name of various clubs and organisations are given to these illegal sellers through a syndicate; when you buy tickets from these sellers, the money will go into the pocket of some corrupt member of BFF, so stand in front of the gate and buy tickets from the legal seller, as they are bound to deposit that money in cash; but there is a fun thing here: if you go to buy tickets from the legal booth, you will see the legal ticket seller cum gate man will take money from you and say take the ticket from that person; since the poster regularly watches matches in the ground, he has seen this situation many times, and you understand, the legal ticket man is also involved in it; you will not want to take complimentary tickets, and as a conscious citizen, you should ensure whether your money is going to BFF's treasury; and the poster's idea is that as many tickets as are sold, that is counted as spectator attendance, and on the AFC website or Wiki, you will see the Bangladesh-Sri Lanka match attendance was only 1500 people; is that really so; the poster's idea is that on that day, there were at least 3500+ spectators, and BFF probably doesn't count the complimentary ticket people, so a wrong image is going to the world this way; since watching football by going to the ground is a part of loving the country, please don't let it be polluted; P.S.: if you are capable, is it very difficult to watch a match by buying a ticket for 20 taka; you will see various organisations giving complimentary tickets to watch matches with them, and you can watch with the organisation, but if you really want to participate in the country's development, without causing a loss to BFF, buying an authorised ticket from an authorised counter will be right; we all should play a role, however small, to go on the path of development.
