I expect a win because we are not going to Tajikistan for holiday; the question is that any away match is always a hard one because it is not your home match, but sometimes it can be positive because the players feel no pressure like they do in a home match; the physiological action can also be different from the home match; we know Tajikistan will try everything to win, but we are not scared at all; I think our team has earned some self-confidence in the last few months; we will go there and play our own match — Fabio Lopez; courtesy: The Daily Star.
Because football matches are organised only in Dhaka, football is getting 'covered' (Dhaka).

Today, the football team's Tajikistan journey is also a mission to change history; playing seven matches against Tajikistan, one win is beside two draws, and of the four defeats, two were at the opponent's ground; in this World Cup qualifiers, in 2003, 2-0, in 2007, 5-0; this time, going to the Tajiks' den, can history be changed; yesterday at the press conference, Bangladesh captain Mamunul Islam himself said, 'This is also our mission to change history'; to play their sixth match in the 2018 World Cup qualifiers, the Bangladesh team is leaving for Tajikistan today at 11 am, and to adapt to the environment, going a bit early this time; in the World Cup qualifiers, Bangladesh's gain in the previous five matches is 1 point, and the only real possibility of winning a match was against these Tajiks, at home, but on 16 June, after going ahead, De Kruif's Bangladesh lost the win due to the disease of conceding a goal at the last moment (1-1); winning the return match against the Tajiks on 12 November is not easy, and being able to draw will be a much better result; Tajikistan has taken two points by drawing with Bangladesh and Kyrgyzstan, and this time, the Bangladesh-Tajik return match will almost decide the fourth place in the five-team group; the Tajiks are ahead, and the intense cold there is also a big opponent for Bangladesh; the temperature in the capital Dushanbe had come down to 6 degrees yesterday, and on the match day, the minimum may be 7, but last month, Bangladesh conquered Kyrgyzstan's biting cold; Bangladesh, trailing by one goal till 88 minutes, finally lost 2-0 to the Kyrgyz; there is a bit of self-satisfaction in the coach and players that Bangladesh played the match well, and that too is a companion on this tour; at home, Mamunul and co. played attacking against the Tajiks, and in the return match, handling the defence is the main mantra; coach Fabio Lopez is painting a picture of victory in that, 'Yes, I respect the opponent, but whatever the strategy, I am going for a win'; Tajikistan's ranking is 160, Bangladesh's is 180, and Lopez wants to bridge this gap with morale; pointing to Mamunul sitting beside him, he joked, 'He is my best soldier; if they fight, everything is possible', and laughing, he patted the captain's back and teased a bit; if they win this match, the possibility of entering the Asia Cup qualifiers can be kept alive, and the captain said in a serious voice, 'The win against Tajikistan is very much needed for us; this win can take us a bit ahead to get the Asia Cup qualifiers' ticket'; the match in Dushanbe is on turf, and Bangladesh's footballers play well on turf; in Bhutan's Kings Cup and Kolkata's Yuva Bharati in the IFA Shield, Sheikh Jamal excelled on artificial grass grounds; Mamunul was saying, 'We hope to do well on Tajikistan's turf'; but how is the team; two experienced players, Emily and Zahid, were not taken, and due to card problems and injuries, Topu and Mishu are out, but defenders Nasir Uddin and Sohel Rana have returned after recovering from injuries; before leaving, the coach wanted to 'see' the team a bit more, so he made the national team play a preparation match yesterday against Arambagh, a second-tier team in the professional league; at the Bangabandhu Stadium, the national team could not win that match (goalless draw); Lopez's explanation: 'In the last few days, the players have worked very hard; they are a bit tired'; Arambagh coach Kamal Babu also said the same thing, 'The team is not bad, but they seemed tired'; Mamunul wanted to keep the confidence by saying, 'It's nothing, everything will be fine'; the captain has made a pledge to change history in Tajikistan; but what is surprising is that on this important tour, there is no goalkeeper coach, yet there is a BFF observer.

The Tajikistan match is the very last chance to avoid the play-off; when the poster first saw the format for playing the Asia Cup, he thought our team at least has the ability to play the Asia Cup, since it is a 24-country cup, and we were in a better position than this in the last World Cup qualifiers or the Asia Cup; he jumped a lot; the Asia Cup, the biggest tournament of the world's biggest continent, and imagining Bangladesh on the Asia Cup stage thrilled him, as this is how we are in the same group as Iran and Japan in the Asia Cup; the whole people of Bangladesh, the way they watch a foreign country's World Cup or Euro Cup, are waiting with the same or even more excitement to watch Bangladesh's match; reality and dreams are different things; Kyrgyzstan came first and slapped hard; wake up, Arif, see the reality; how much a few players playing in leagues in Europe and naturalised players change a team; a 3-1 loss in front of his eyes at the Bangabandhu Stadium, and the achievement is Mamun's corner, which was impossibly beautiful, while the points account is empty; then the Tajik match, and we play well, but God knows if any country in the world has such spineless strikers, with miss after miss, and mentally crippled too; after going 1-0 ahead, how badly and visibly they become defensive; can't believe it; the result: a foul near the D-box by Emily and a free kick, and that's where the dream of three points ended; well, are Jordan's players' passes and dribbling beautiful, or Bangladesh's; if you base it on one match, the poster will say we are ahead; how does Jewel miss like this after cutting three-four players, even cutting the goalkeeper; he doesn't know; that miss by Emily; uff; Mamun's corner would have gone into the goal box anyway, it seems; Topu heads over, and it looks like our Topu cleared for Jordan, and they, with some damn referee's wrong decision, get a penalty and suddenly score a goal and snatch the match from our hands; many times, the scorecard doesn't show the ground performance, and those who didn't watch the match will never understand; what trouble Bangladesh put Jordan's famous defenders in, and how beautifully Mamun took control of the midfield; what is the benefit of all this; the result is the last word; when we can't even go to the U19 Asia Cup despite getting competitors like Bhutan and Sri Lanka at age level, the poster feels like reciting Abul Hossain's poem, 'I have understood, it won't happen with me'; still, we have to stay positive, and we have tried; in defeat after defeat, bad luck, insult, and childishness at club level, we haven't given up dreams, and even when we had to stay positive about the country as champions in corruption again and again, what is this; staying positive about football, where there should have been long-term planning at every level from our age level; BFF, the world's biggest hair-pulling institution, has disappointed again and again, and we can't even play the AFC Cup due to mismanagement; the ranking is on the way to touching 200, and if the poster were a communist, dictatorial ruler, he might have turned off football in the country in anger; what shame is there in being behind 179 countries; quotes from Jibanananda Das and Kazi Nazrul Islam follow.

entities.name: Bangladesh Football Walking Around the Dreams

posts.summary: The poster couldn't see newspapers much; he saw a post on Facebook: the Bangladesh national team reportedly drew with Arambagh; is the story true; with Arambagh in the end; the poster thinks even if the Bangladesh football walking around the dream group's XI played against the national team, they would draw; not only that, with the pathetic condition of our strikers, even if it were an empty-field XI vs the national team, the result would still be 0-0; there would be no one as a player in the empty field; still...

Do you know what's a very funny thing; we don't even have an official Facebook page; a few days ago, the Sheikh Kamal International Club Cup ended, and along with many teams, our Abahani also played in the tournament, and there were two Indian teams too, and almost everyone knows Indian supporters made a lot of noise about the tournament; naturally, they asked us about our club, and many asked the poster, 'Dada, tell us about Abahani; what is their condition now?' and he told them as much as he could; after that, they asked for our official Facebook page and website, and they asked about the fanbase; the sad thing is he could only talk about the fanbase, and he had to say with shame that we don't have a Facebook page or a website; they were surprised: a club of this era and no Facebook page; is it true; well, it takes two minutes to make a page, and with just $1, a page can be boosted, and Abahani's fans are not few, and everyone would like it; there are many web developers who are Abahani fans; won't they make a website for little money; and why will it cost little money; at most, four-five thousand will be needed, and buying a hosting and a domain is the cost; if we do this much, will the Mahabharata be impure; if done, there will be more publicity, and if not in Asia, at least the people of South Asia will be able to recognise Dhaka Abahani, one of South Asia's best clubs; as a fan, can't he hope for this much; off-post talk: fortunately, one day the poster talked to Rupu Sir, meaning Abahani's manager Satyajit Das Rupu, and told him about the page, and he said he will look into it, but 2 months have passed, and Sir hasn't looked; and the poster thinks no club in Bangladesh has an official page; Feni's two are unofficial fan pages, Sheikh Jamal's is also not official, and as far as he knows, Chittagong Abahani's is also unofficial.

2 or 3 months ago, if the poster recalls, in a newspaper he read that Bangladesh's former coach De Kruif may sign in to a Bangladeshi club; so, does anyone know anything about it; any update regarding it?
Will Soccer League UK buy the rights of the B(D)PL; what is the condition of the BSSL; has anything progressed?
Arambagh's coach said that due to the players' tiredness and playing in other positions, the national team's footballers could not play their best game in the training match.

The poster had a lot of hope; not only him, but every football fan in the country had hope that this time, at least, we will cross the World Cup qualifiers; he left Australia aside, and with the rest of the teams, we can hope for a win, but what happened; in five matches, one draw and four defeats, and the World Cup... our Asia Cup hope is also dying, but what can we do; this is perhaps fate; you know, that day he cried, and really, after the home match against Kyrgyzstan, he truly cried, and perhaps many fans cried; anyway, is hoping our fault; as many times as we hope about our own country, each time they make us cry, but still, we don't give up hope; earlier too, he said once that those of us who work more or less on the country's football online are surviving completely on lies; if something happens, we have to lie; if someone asks after the match, 'Hey Tasin, what's the condition of your team; I heard they lost again?' then, showing a hundred and one false reasons behind the loss, we prove our own team, meaning our Bangladesh national team, to be the best; sometimes bad refereeing, sometimes injury, and sometimes talking about the opposing team's rough play, we save the team from being disgraced; but how many more days with false reasons, brother; the poster and many supporters like him have given up hope for the next match, you know; we are no longer hoping that we will win against Tajikistan; we only hope this much: that after losing, we don't need false reasons this time, so that we can say we played well; we played very well; can we hope this much from them, or will hoping be a fault?
Kyrgyzstan vs Bangladesh — YouTube link.

Ladies and gentlemen, let's have a minute's silence for our dream of the AFC Cup; the Bangabandhu Gold Cup will be played in the 3rd week of January, and most possibly the final in the 1st week of February (same as last year), and in the 1st week of February, Sheikh Jamal will have their match, so Sheikh Jamal won't or may not get their regular players.
They better finish this tournament by January and declare the transfer window in February; #RoadToAFCCup.
Is the Bangladesh-Tajikistan match at 5 pm Bangladesh time; the match is at 17:00 local time.

Throughout November, there will be World Cup qualifier matches; in December, there will be SAFF; in January, there will be the Bangabandhu Gold Cup, and along with that will be Sheikh Jamal's AFC Cup mission; by the time this ends, it will be February, and then there may be 15 days' rest, and in the meantime, the 2nd tier matches of the Bangladesh professional league will be fully completed; and as March comes, the BFF election will start, and by the time it ends, it will be the first week of May '16; in the first meeting of the newly elected committee, everything for the new season may come; this seems to the poster to be Bangladesh football's next 6 months' calendar; if there is any mistake, please look at it with a forgiving eye.

At the Faridpur Sheikh Jamal Stadium, the match between Gerda Union and Ambikapur Union is going on; an inter-union football tournament, and 30 minutes have passed, a very exciting match; bypassing quite a few foreigners, Abahani's, oops, Gerda's Mamun Mia, Ambikapur's Prantosh Kumar, the main point of excitement of five and a half thousand spectators is Ambikapur's Enamul; everyone's eyes are on this tall and hairy player; not Muktijoddha or Bangladesh's, but Ambikapur's Enamul, look carefully; really; is a national team player, one of the league's top scorers, in such need that he comes to play at the union level; really?
Name: Abdul Baten Komol; age: 28; position: Forward, Midfield (Left and Right); national team appearance: 20 matches and scored 1 goal; club: Dhaka Abahani Ltd; video link.
2 more days to go.

Coach Maruful Haque will be given a reception by his former club Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club; this was said by Sheikh Jamal Club's boss Manjur Kader; whatever he does, he does some work which is definitely praiseworthy; Maruful Haque first showed his class by coaching for Mohammedan in the 2008-09 season, then in the 2010-11 season, he was Muktijoddha's coach, then one by one, becoming Sheikh Russel and Sheikh Jamal's coach, and now he is in charge as Sheikh Russel's coach; and his coaching career started with Badda Jagoroni Club.
Mamunul Islam gets his position back; Rony, Toklis or Sohel Rana may be in the wing position, and Abdul Baten Komol to defender from winger — Kaler Kantho link.

Another Bangla-wash in cricket: Bangladesh won the 3-match series against Zimbabwe 3-0; congratulations to the Bangladesh cricket team; and tomorrow, the Bangladesh football team will take the field against Tajikistan at Tajikistan's ground; God willing, like cricket, we will also get a good result in football, and God willing, points will come in tomorrow's match; Joy Bangla #RoarwithbengalTigers.
At the press conference before the match against the Tajiks, coach Lopez and handsome and cute Jamal Bhai; crush is not allowed.

In the World Cup qualifiers match, tomorrow's match opponent for Bangladesh is Tajikistan; when going to play an away match against Tajikistan, somehow a fear comes inside the mind, but with the fear, the poster gets a courage to win; and at home, there is one point against Tajikistan; in the 2010 World Cup qualifiers in 2007, at home, after leading 1-0 at first, Bangladesh drew in the later part of the second half due to the referee's wrong decision; that day, the poster left the gallery with a lot of pain, and he didn't abuse the referee less that day; but in the away match, playing with all the adversities, Bangladesh lost 5-0, and with that, all dreams were broken; again in 2015, Bangladesh in an away match, the opponent is the same Tajikistan; the time has come to take revenge, with a new team combination and a new coach's new theory; the poster hopes at least one point will come to us; Joy Bangla #RoarwithBengalTigers.
Good news: tomorrow's Bangladesh-Tajikistan away match will be shown live by Channel Nine from 6 pm.
Upgrading our league 60% completed; 40% loading.
Komol Bhai, what did he miss; and both goals were conceded due to the defence's mistake.

A horrible kind of defence; there is no one in the team like Nasir Chowdhury, no Yeasin; is Kesto Kumar in the main team; can Komol play at left-back in defence; is he the best player of Bangladesh above midfield; the fear the poster had; and leaving office work to watch the match, is this the result; brother, still can't foreigners be taken into the team?

The German FA (DFB) is set to appoint national hockey team coach Markus Weise to work for its forthcoming academy; Weise, 52, has won back-to-back gold medals at the last two Olympic games with the German men's team, adding to his 2004 triumph with the women's hockey team; he will be the second hockey coach to work for DFB; football is a science, and we are still shouting for a trainer at club level; shame.

The four is complete; how many more we concede, only God knows; against Australia, they conceded 5; conceding 5 against them at Tajikistan's ground is our old work; did the fear the poster had come true; what is Mamun doing in his position; there is no plan on the field, and the blame will fall on the coach.

Today, the poster realised only one thing: dreaming is forbidden for us; in a post before, he said he doesn't expect anything in this match, but in some corner of his mind, there was a small hope that maybe we will win the match, but keeping hope is like a sin, and even a respectable loss is not deserved; and why should there be a respectable loss for us; what are we; we are football fans of a cricket country, and not of Real-Barça-Brazil-Argentina, but fans of Bangladesh; what big fools we are, tell me; yes, right, we don't deserve a win, or even a respectable loss, and may it never come to our fate; but still, what can we do; we are Bangladeshis, brother, and whatever else we stop, we don't stop hoping about our own country; yes, not 5-0, even if it's 10-0, the poster is still with the Bangladesh team; it will happen in the next match; #roar_with_The_Bengal_tigers #go_tigers #go_bangladesh.

The players don't mark; then what is the defenders' work; after the rain, the turf becomes slippery, and no one could run, as they were running in fear, and if they fall on the turf, they will get hurt — they are afraid to charge too, and even when they charged, they were moving away; even Sohel was stiff; the weather is a problem, but so many goals because of that; why didn't BFF give long socks, full-sleeve jerseys and gloves; there is nothing to say about fitness, as this is the fault of the clubs and the players; if one with the ball runs faster than one without the ball, that player should have a rope around his neck; football is a game for the brave, and if you play with fear, wear bangles; if the players don't give 100%, what will the coach feed them?

The Bangladesh football team lost 5-0; many will say many things, and they will say the turf on the ground, the cold, and the rain on top of that, but for all this, you went 6 days early to adapt to the weather; and in the match, who was playing in which position, no one had any idea; many will say, what is the coach doing; will the coach now go down to the field and play; Mamunul Bhai, you played in your position today, and are you our team's best player; and we got a different kind of Jamal; if Topu and Raju were there, it could have been different; brothers, leave the grouping in the team; we cannot accept losing to Tajikistan like this; it really hurts when the poster sees us falling behind in the ranking; it may not hurt you, but it hurts us; still, he will keep supporting Bangladesh football; and now, when will the criticism of the coach start; this is our religion; will the coach himself do grouping now; and seeing this criticism on Facebook, tomorrow some criticism of the coach will be seen in some media.

Bangladesh 0, Tajikistan 5; some of you guys may be sad or depressed by now, but the poster wants to say one thing: do you all know 'Sher Shah Suri' or 'Sher Khan'; he lived during the Mughal period of Humayun, and he faced the Mughal Emperor 3 times (Humayun's army); in the year 1532, Sher Shah's men were defeated badly, and then Sher Khan recovered from his failure and crushed Humayun's army in the year 1539, 'The Battle of Chausa', and in 1540, 'The Battle of Bilgram'; bottom line: learn from your mistakes, have patience, and you will surely win like how Sher Khan won; what the poster wants you all guys is not to panic, and let's accept our defeat in a positive way and look ahead for a positive future, and figure out our weakness; Bangladesh isn't good at away matches, against Australia score 5-0, Jordan 4-0, Kyrgyzstan 2-0 and Tajikistan 5-0, and no goals scored at away matches by us; he hopes BFF will sit down with coach Lopez and plan out everything, what is to be done and how it's going to be, and aim for winning the SAFF Championship; cheers.
Bare YouTube link.
Next season's transfer window date will be given in the coming week, and Sheikh Jamal management be like...
Dhaka Mohammedan winger Mohammed Ibrahim, jersey number 19; #TransferRumors: Chittagong Abahani is all set to sign him for the upcoming season; good luck, lad.
Emoticon only.
The moment you realise Emily is only the one who scored for Bangladesh in the World Cup qualifiers.

Let the poster give an example of football with Bangladesh cricket: in 2014, when cricket was going through a very bad time, exactly then, by whitewashing Zimbabwe in all formats, cricket started giving its best form; our football is in the same condition now, as many matches have passed with no win, and no goals at the forwards' feet, so one thing can be done: let's play a tournament with Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bhutan and Laos, we will become champions and regain our morale, and we will also be able to beat Australia and Jordan, and we will also be able to play in the Asia Cup; the poster expects everyone's opinion.

Well, suppose the agreement between Soccer League UK and BFF happens, and BFF agrees to all the terms, but will the clubs agree; Soccer League will definitely say to become professional, but will they be able to become professional; all the poster's fear is about the clubs.
Wahed Ahmed, Dhaka Abahani's forward — YouTube link.
Bangladesh vs Tajikistan 1-1 (home match), 0-5 (away match); Bangladesh vs Australia 0-5 (away match); home match score...

Tomorrow, the Australia football team is not coming to Bangladesh; they will come on the day before the match, 16 November, and before the Bangladesh match, they will practice in Singapore; and the players are responsible for the loss against Tajikistan, says BFF boss Kazi Salahuddin, who wants to give more time to Italian coach Fabio Lopez.
Hurt me, I won't be broken; stop me, I won't listen; Red and Green, I am limitless; it's a tough me; I am Bangladesh.
Bare Alokito Bangladesh article link.
Nothing much to say; BFF needs to be more professional.
3 days to go; let's do this.
What has Jugantor started; today's sports page has a horrible report about football, and it ruined the poster's mood.

After the home match against Australia, when is the match against Jordan, and after that, the play-off that will happen — has a date been given for that; 17th is Australia, after that, the China tour, then SAFF, then the Bangabandhu Cup, later the SA Games and the AFC Cup; what is the schedule after that?
Kruif hasn't got a job even after so many days; he still goes around sharing what he's doing in Bangladesh; Abahani, please give him a job, please, please.

Recently, BFF invited some teams to play in the Bangabandhu Gold Cup; they invited teams like Myanmar, Afghanistan, Sri Lanka and some Middle East teams; till now, Sri Lanka confirmed their spot, and the poster believes BFF has requested other teams to inform them before 15 or within 15 November; it's going to be interesting to see who all will take part in this tournament.
According to Alokito Bangladesh, the UK Soccer League management will visit Dhaka Mohammedan, Brothers Union and Rahmatganj MFS.
Tomi Juric and Tom Rogic have been ruled out of Australia's World Cup qualifier against Bangladesh due to injuries — The Daily Star.
We grapple the crown of Victor; we are the untamed Bangladesh.
For the match against Australia, forward Zahid Hossain, Topu Barman and Mishu got a call to the national team's camp; best wishes.
Hoping for something good and positive.

Australia did no less drama over security in the last 2 months; first the cricket team didn't come, then the football team also wouldn't come; later, after sending their security team and fixing everything, they were supposed to come on Saturday, but later, showing various excuses, they will come on Monday afternoon and, after playing the match on Tuesday, will go straight to the airport without going to the hotel; they will come for 30 hours; not only that, on the match day, no one can enter Bangabandhu without a ticket, and the roads will be closed anyway; brother, there was a lot of speculation about this match, and today it seems BFF should have organised the match in an empty stadium and closed all the roads for 2 days; seriously, now it's getting a bit too much; just because we are a poor country, is all this happening; Zimbabwe played and went, nothing happened, and ahead, the U-19 Cricket World Cup will also be in Bangladesh, so why so much about the Australia match?
Veteran winger Zahid Hossain, who got a late call-up, has so far declined to join the squad — The Daily Star.
Jibon in action, jersey number 10, and in the meantime (RIP video theme song) — YouTube link.
Bare Prothom Alo article link: Mamunul's closed-door practice.
Happy birthday to Hasan Al Mamun, one of the best defenders of Bangladesh (as the poster has seen); many best wishes for Hasan Al Mamun Bhaiya on his birthday.

Tomorrow is going to be the Bangladesh team's biggest match on home soil; yes, the poster is talking about the Bangladesh vs Australia match; the last match we lost 5-0 (against Tajikistan), and against Australia in the away match too, the margin was the same, but this time, perhaps we will try to reduce the margin, because, first, home conditions, a familiar ground, our own spectators, and along with that, perhaps Zahid, who missed the Tajikistan match and played exceptionally in the Sheikh Kamal Gold Cup, will return to the team; a loss by a small margin can be expected, what do you say?

Around 10 footballers went to Sheikh Jamal club today for some meeting or program; the poster is not interested to know whether they broke the rules or not, he is just glad to know Sheikh Jamal retained 10 players; the AFC Cup dream isn't over yet.

Our sports minister is the Bangladesh football team's ex-captain, we all know; do you know, he is a very good shooter, and once he went to the football pitch with a rifle; he is more talented than Asif, the poster thinks; Asif is the man who won gold at the Commonwealth Games in shooting for Bangladesh; oh, wait, Arif Khan Joy is a legend boxer too, and he used to do his boxing practice in real life; the poster would suggest to the Bangladesh government to rename the Mohammed Ali boxing stadium as the Arif Khan Joy boxing stadium; proud of you, sir, you are such a multi-talented guy; #Arif_means_talents #Our_legend; news link: bdnews24.
Positive mentality; cheers — Kaler Kantho link.
Bangladesh possible line-up and formation — Socceroos website link.

0-5 Tajikistan, 0-2 Kyrgyzstan, 0-4 Jordan, 0-5 Australia, 0-0 Malaysia: the Bangladesh team's last five match results; in five matches, against four losses, the number of wins is zero and one draw; today's match needs a win very much, but a win against Australia is impossible, so our hope is the team will give a respectable result today, because three of the last four losses were by a big margin; #support_GREENandRED.

Yes, we lost today's match too, 4-0; team hat-trick; but you know, after the match, every supporter's face had a smile; the poster doesn't know about others, but he jumped after the match; there is only one reason: the second half, as we kept a team like Australia stuck for the full 48 minutes, and Shahidul, what saves; all the credit for keeping Australia to 4 goals today goes to this wall of ours; and Hemonto-da attacked a few times, Mamun Bhai came down from midfield and handled the defence, Raju Bhai was bright in midfield, and Jamal Boss, as always, #King; everyone will say the team lost, don't shout, but the poster will say today's loss was like a win; #REDandGREEN #roar_with_the_bengal_tigers.

The poster just wants BFF to keep Lopez for more 2-3 years (not to treat him as they did to our former coach De Kruif); he is really impressed with today's performance, as we played good, and now before facing Jordan at their home, we hope we will play some friendlies against some Middle East countries like UAE or Iraq; whatever, it's just beginning, not the end; next mission SAFF.

Today's match's best defender was Komol; how can it be if he is so nervous; no new player is needed, and after the China tour, just add a psychiatrist till SAFF; and players, the poster hopes you understood your position even after playing with good players; those who get a salary above 20 lakh — please spend 1 lakh a year for your own career: nutritionist, gym and meditation; it will be good for you and for the country too.

The poster really requests BFF to renew the contract with the full coaching staff till March, shift the date of the Bangabandhu Cup to February after the SA Games, otherwise ensure that the U-23 team and Sheikh Jamal will play the tournament in January, add a psychiatrist with the coaching team till the SA Games, and don't open the transfer window till 15 February; this is the only way we can ensure the SA Games, AFC Cup and World Cup qualifier.
Please don't use any bad words or slang; if anyone uses it, he/she will be banned from this group — Admin.

Truly, Bangladesh played well today, and Australia was lucky with one handball and one clean offside; well done, coach Fabio Lopez, you have made many changes to the team, and you played very well, but the team can't give something good; by the way, can't some senior players be dropped?

Look at today's Asian region World Cup qualifiers results; the biggest news is Kyrgyzstan beating Jordan 1-0, showing the biggest surprise: World Cup – AFC Qualification, Group A: FT Timor-Leste 0-10 Saudi Arabia, FT Malaysia 1-2 UAE; Group B: FT Bangladesh 0-4 Australia, FT Kyrgyzstan 1-0 Jordan; Group C: FT Bhutan 0-3 Qatar, FT Hong Kong 0-0 China; Group D: FT Guam 0-6 Iran, FT Turkmenistan 2-1 Oman; Group E: FT Singapore 1-2 Syria, FT Cambodia 0-2 Japan; Group F: FT Taiwan 0-2 Iraq.

There is a difference between playing well and defending well, the poster guesses; how is not being able to create any real threat and taking the ball into the opponent's territory only a few times good football; because of the conditions and unfamiliarity with the ground, for some reason the poster felt they couldn't play their natural game; in the Perth match, they played more pacey football, and the one who was creating the most chances in the first half was taken off at the start of the second half; but it is also true that the players put in much more effort than the previous day, and the defensive work was also better.

Some kangaroo fans of the kangaroo country watched the match today; their work was entirely like kangaroos, and in between, there was good sledging with the local spectators, but it was enjoyable between the spectators of the two countries.

No one noticed that today, struggling in the Central Asian freezing cold conditions, Jordan and Oman lost to Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan respectively; and we are Bangladesh; what happened on 28 October 2007 also happened this year on 12 November — a 5-0 loss in unbearable cold; BFF is busy with the Sheikh Kamal Cup, and what was the benefit; of the 14 who played against Tajikistan, 7 had no match time since the Kyrgyz match 1 month ago; if sending the team 6 days early helped, there would be no such thing as a FIFA friendly in the world; in the last World Cup qualifiers too, BFF made this mistake before the match against Lebanon.

Two hours before kick-off, the police administration postponed the Germany vs Netherlands match due to a security issue; the match's venue was Hanover, and on the same issue, the Belgium vs Spain match was cancelled earlier; #We_can_be_proud_of_Bangladesh's_security.
Bare mentions of Samrat Mohim Talukder, Rahik Sumail and Maksud Haque.

Quite a few sponsors were found in the 2nd tier of the professional league; now let's see how the 2nd tier league goes.

Sheikh Jamal boss Manjur Kader will step away from BFF; there is no working environment in BFF, so Manjur Kader will leave, and he will not remain as the head of the district league committee, and he will not come in the upcoming election either.
Bangladesh 2-3 (Hanthawady United), Myanmar.
What else is there to say?

The poster has no respect left at all for the man Lopez; firstly, in his life, he has never seen a coach who, after conceding 4-5 goals, gives various excuses and says we played well; secondly, he has never seen any coach in the world who beats his own drum, and you can see that if you go to his page; thirdly, after conceding 11 goals in three matches in the recent World Cup qualifiers, a loss against the 7th-placed club in Myanmar's league; so, whatever anyone says, in his judgement, he is a third-class coach; lastly, he wants to say that this time at SAFF too, there is probably no hope, and like the last two times, they will be eliminated from the first round.
#TrollPost: Lopez fans' reaction after listening they lost 3-2 today.

The poster won't say anything; isn't his contract term till SAFF; in this time, with BFF's full support, full coaching staff, staying in the country the whole time, and playing regular matches, he wants to see how much Bangladesh can improve and where it takes them in the ranking; at least in the previous coach's era, he can say we lost playing well, and in some matches, luck was also not good.

The poster thinks justice wasn't made with our former coach Lodewijk de Kruif; we had a fighting mentality at some point of his coaching spell (except in some matches like against the Socceroos at their home), and he was just cementing his playing style and tactics after many experiments, but he was sacked after the 'disgusting' Aussie defeat; in the poster's personal opinion, that was an early move by BFF, and another 'hurried approach' by BFF was to replace him with Fabio Lopez; we should've gone with an interim coach and searched for a 'deserving' and 'appropriate' man, who could solve our current problems and take lessons from the past; the poster knows Mr. Lopez hasn't got enough time to prove his worthiness yet, but he has got 'full freedom' from the authority, and he must use this to prove himself useful to our football, though he made some experiments with that freedom, but some of the experiments were 'terrible' to him; there's a saying 'Don't mess with the basics', and that could be a message to Mr. Lopez from his end; good luck; N.B.: these are his personal opinion, it may conflict with yours, and he has full respect for your opinion too; constructive thoughts are welcomed.
Our best result after Lopez took the charge: a draw against Arambagh.

Was playing this tournament in China so urgent; after losing today, the manager said all the players are tired, so what did everyone go to China to do; tired like this, they will play ahead and become even more tired, then what will happen, will we become seventh at SAFF again; coming back, will we say we are tired from playing continuously; ahead is the league, and many will play saving their legs, which happened in the 2013 SAFF, and this is not new, it has been coming since the Mughal era; later, what will happen: the coach is a useless one, and in BFF too, many dramas are going on.

#Urgent_post: In Sylhet's 'Kajolshah', blood (O-ve) is needed for a father; help gather a blood donor by copying/sharing as much as possible, as a life will be saved by the blood you give; for a cancer-affected father's leg operation, 2 bags of 'O negative' blood are needed by 8 pm today (21-11-15); place: Osmani Medical College Hospital; mobile: 01710937832.
Chittagong 3rd division football league result: Rafa Club 4-2 MH Sporting Club.

Off-topic: Bangladesh 2(3)-2(2) Oman; second win against Oman in the tournament, and the journey of glory is still going on; Bangladesh is going to take on Malaysia in their next match to ensure 5th place of the tournament; a loss against Japan at the quarter-final destroyed the dream of playing the semi-final, and after a lot of days, the poster felt deeply pained for a match in the hockey, football or cricket field; anyway, becoming the 5th/6th best team in Asian hockey isn't a bad result; thank you, hockey team, you made us smile through the month; better luck next time; #we_did_not_learn_to_give_up; by the way, do you know, the hockey league is stopped in Bangladesh for a couple of years for some management problems, but our guys never stopped showing brilliant performances at the international level; most of the players do not earn money of livelihood from this game, and even after that, they are awesome; after facing this much problem, this team beat one of the giants of Asian hockey, South Korea; #Cholo_Bangladesh.
BREAKING: The Pakistan Football Federation has decided not to send their national football team for next month's SAFF Championship in India.

The poster doesn't understand the matter: did Bangladesh lose to the Myanmar national team or to their club; on BFF's page and in a newspaper too, he saw it written that the opponent was the national team.

posts.summary: In the Yunnan ASEAN International Open Football Tournament, Bangladesh lost their 2nd match too; against China's Lijiang club, Bangladesh lost 2-1 with the side-bench players; Monaem Khan Raju got a red card at one stage, and Bangladesh played with 10 men; Bangladesh, trailing 1-0 in the first half, brought back equality with Aminur Rahman Sajib's goal, but after conceding a goal in the 85th minute, the team had to leave the field with a loss; so, under Fabio Lopez, Bangladesh's best result so far is the goalless draw against Arambagh.
AFC Award Night 2015 nominees for Player of the Year (men): Ahmed Khalil (UAE), Omar Abdulrahman (UAE), Zheng Zhi (China).
The Pakistan football team withdrew their name from the SAFF Championship.

Even after 24 hours have passed since the instruction to show cause within 48 hours to Manjur Kader and Lokman Hossain, neither of them received the letter; by the way, in that day's incident, is manager Babu a saint; why didn't he stop them; BFF didn't say anything to him?

The poster was saying from a few days ago that a new drama is coming in Bangladesh football; Kader Sahib, who was the BFF boss's favourite person, and against him a show-cause notice, along with Mohammedan's Lokman Sahib too, but why; after being in the BFF camp, how do the players go out in a group without saying anything; was the team management sleeping; did they know nothing; and why did they let them go; if you can't control the team, leave the responsibility; and to the players, is the club bigger than the national team; and before such a big match, with what conscience do they go; the main fault is of these players; Kader Sahib probably thought that the day after the match, everyone will go to China, so let me sit with everyone for 1 hour and discuss the AFC; if he didn't get permission, he couldn't have done this work; whatever he does, to the poster he seems professional; and what improvement will you make in football by doing a showy drama; everyone understands everything.

The poster saw some parts of the full-match highlights of the Maldives-China match; Maldives' playing style now felt like the style we play under Lopez, but their tactical sense and player quality are better; the poster is becoming more disappointed day by day about going to the next round at SAFF by overtaking them and Afghanistan.

Tomorrow, in the Chittagong 3rd division football league, in their first match, Chittagong City United (Noapara Lions) Club will take the field against Lohagara Upazila Sports Association at 3:30 pm at the Bandar Stadium; come to the ground and support Chittagong United (Noapara Lions) Club.
Bangladesh streak continues, and the Undertaker will be like...

In the CJKC-CDFA Banoful Third Division Football League, three matches were held on the second day; in these matches, Rising Star Junior, Agrani Sangha and Raujan Upazila Sports Association won; yesterday, at the Shaheed Shamsuzzaman Bandar Stadium, in the morning, Rising Star Junior defeated Chandanaish Upazila Sports Association 3-2; Belayet scored 2 and Manjurul 1 for the winning team, and Chandanaish's Khalif alone scored 2 goals; in the afternoon, Agrani Sangha defeated Mirsarai Upazila Sports Association by Alamgir's goal; in the evening match, with Shahin Alam's hat-trick, Raujan Upazila Sports Association won 3-1 against Kallol Sangha Green.
The poster was waiting for this news — Kaler Kantho link.

A BFF person, unwilling to reveal his name, said, 'The BFF president is thinking about a local coach for SAFF by bidding farewell to Lopez; apart from performance, questions have also arisen about Lopez's team management; the president is not interfering in the coach's freedom, he is only seeing whether any positive change is happening inside the team, and as soon as he returns from China, he will talk to him about this'; if Lopez is bid farewell, the national team will be handed to a local coach in his place; in that case, it is known that Sheikh Russel coach Maruful Haque and Chittagong Abahani coach Shafiqul Islam Manik are being thought of, and Bangladesh's SAFF mission will start in one of their hands; source — Kaler Kantho.

What the poster was trying to explain for so long; from Kaler Kantho: in the meantime, in the World Cup qualifiers' three matches, leaving aside the strong Australia and Kyrgyzstan, there was a bit of hope about the Tajikistan match in comparison, but Bangladesh, who drew with this opponent in Dhaka, returned from Dushanbe with the shame of 5 goals; if we go by the coach's words, all hopes were washed away in the cold-rain; in the World Cup qualifiers, all the teams in the group are above Bangladesh in the ranking, so the performance stage was difficult, but in China's Yunnan province's unknown tournament; in this ongoing tournament, Lopez's team is also losing against club teams; after losing the first match against Myanmar's club team, they held up travel fatigue as a shield, and yesterday, after losing against the local Yunnan province's unknown Lijiang club, they are talking about biased refereeing; ten years ago, this fiction was quite common in football, when the team's coach-manager blamed 'referee, goalpost and bad luck' to make a match story; in Lopez's era, those days have returned; the problem is, this story is not melting the hearts of the current federation officials.
#lopez_out.
#lopez_out.
Let's organise a friendly match with the members of this group: Kruif fans vs Kruif haters; it will be good.

At least in the matter of appointing a coach, BFF's arbitrariness should be stopped; the Argentine Football Federation's relationship with Diego Maradona was very bad, but still, they appointed him as the national team's coach, so why won't BFF appoint Maruful Haque; at least considering the national team's interest, can't they give Maruful Haque a chance even once?

From the 26th, the Bangladesh Championship League, known as the second tier, starts; 8 teams will play: 1. Uttar Baridhara, 2. Agrani Bank Limited, 3. Arambagh Krira Sangha, 4. Victoria Sporting Club, 5. Wari Club, 6. Fakirapool Young Men's Club, 7. Motijheel T&T Club, 8. Bangladesh Police; the poster's bet this time is on Arambagh, as they have made a good team, but he will be happy if Wari qualifies for the BPL this time, because Wari is one of the country's most traditional teams; hope for the best.
In the Chittagong 3rd division football league, Lohagara Upazila Sports Association beat Chittagong City United (Noapara Lions) Club 5-0.

From what the poster understood from a few news items, if they lose today, Fabio Lopez will be sacked as soon as he comes to the country; BFF is reportedly thinking of giving the responsibility to youth coach Gonzalo Moreno; the poster doesn't like Fabio Lopez's work at all, but still, he thinks he should be given a chance till SAFF, as sacking him so early is too much.

National team performance under Lopez: 1. Draw against Arambagh KC, a club that plays in the second division of the Bangladesh league; 2. Lose against a low-rank Myanmar Premier League team which is in the relegation zone, and for your kind information, Bangladesh won their last match against Myanmar, and this shitty team can't even manage a draw against their mid-table team; 3. Losing against a Chinese amateur/semi-professional team; 4. 5-0 loss against Tajikistan, where before that match Bangladesh won the last two matches against them; 5. 2-0 loss against Kyrgyzstan; 6. 4-0 loss against Australia; reason behind this performance: 1. The first reason is this guy isn't competent to manage a national team, and he doesn't have such experiences too, and his profile seems so low, while the corrupted and incompetent management of BFF appointed him without thinking about the national team's future; 2. Horrible examination of players in different positions, as it looks like a kid is playing FIFA games — winger to defender, midfielder to forward, etc.; 3. Perhaps our team is not capable of coping with his tactics; just after one month, the SAFF is coming, for which tournament fans wait for years, and the poster is not sure this type of coach can bring a good result in that tournament or not; fans these days are totally hopeless with such performances from the national team, and it will be hard for fans to keep support after these disgusting performances; BFF, don't do a 'BFF' again, and if you sack Lopez, in his position please appoint a local coach ahead of SAFF, because it will be hard for a coach to manage a good team when he is a total stranger to that team and doesn't know the players well; the poster will suggest BFF appoint a coach like Maruful or Manik, under whom these players performed well previously; after SAFF, think about a high-profile foreign coach; #Lopez_out #The_loser_one.

Like hockey, the same kind of drama is about to happen in football too: federation, coach, senior player conflict; the poster hopes the drama will be good; a few days ago, he posted about Ranking Mission 200, and that will now see the light; highlight that news well in a newspaper; joy football's joy.
Will the problem be solved just by changing the coach; if the student is bad, no matter how good a teacher you give, the result won't be good, so change is not a solution.

The poster didn't have to wait long; what he said before happened, as Lopez is a low-standard coach, and expecting anything from this coach is foolishness, while being the national team's coach is not so easy; in the end, Lopez was sacked; thank you to BFF for taking the right decision, and best wishes to the new coach Maruful Haque.
Breaking news: BFF has sacked national football team coach Fabio Lopez due to poor performance; new coach Maruful Haque.
Is there any good place to become a football coach, where I can coach?
Because of this Lopez, BFF dropped goalkeeping coach Christian Schöchler; if he could be brought back, it would be good, as after Christian came, our goalkeepers improved a lot.
Is there any good place to become a football coach, where I can coach?
Is all the blame only on the coach and the players; the BFF president's post is immortal, and he only shows dreams.
The thing that feels best is that a former Barça footballer will work under Maruful Haque; has there ever been a foreign assistant coach under a local coach in Bangladesh before?
Not expected, that.

BFF should look at Chandpur; where the BPL stays spectator-less, today at the Chandpur Club Cup's opening match, the gallery was full with 10-taka tickets; and if we talk about Chandpur's players, we must mention 2/3 of them; Chandpur's boy Sufian has been playing consistently well, and he is called the Messi of Chandpur; so far, the poster has had the fortune to watch 3 of his matches; he is a midfielder who does restless dribbling, through passes, heading, crosses, corner kicks — he is mature in all; the poster thinks he deserves the Dhaka league, and besides, he was the top scorer of the league that ended a few days ago.
Without Lopez, today Bangladesh won 1-0 against the Heaven Club; the win came with the old formation, Mamunul, and Amirul Islam's coaching.
Good luck, coach; hope you do your best.
From France, Olympique Lyon, Argentina's Boca Juniors, and Nacional from Uruguay will support our BSSL league; waiting to hear more names.

According to club sources, several star footballers will reportedly be seen in Dhaka Abahani's jersey; discussions have already been finalised with several star players, and among them, national team captain Mamunul is one, but according to sources, Chittagong Abahani also wants to build a rich team with Mamunul in front; Dhaka Mohammedan also wants to return to its old tradition this time by building a sensational team; in short, all the famous teams are active in building a champion-fight team; source: Daily Janakantha.

Ahead, they say there will be the Bangladesh Super Soccer League, franchise league and how many things in Bangladesh; Soccer League UK, BFF and who else say they will do these together; the poster has no interest in this; his main interest is the upcoming election, as many calculations may change, and something new may happen, or the drama will continue; so, is everyone ready for the election?

The 2nd round matches of the Chittagong 3rd division football league group stage start today at the Shaheed Shamsuzzaman Bandar Stadium: (13. MH Sporting Club vs Customs Excise and VAT Club - 9:15), (14. Mirsarai Upazila Sports Association vs Kallol Sangha Green - 10:45), (15. Baklia Ekadash Junior vs Ullash Club - 1:30), (16. Shahid Shahjahan Sangha vs Noapara Lions Club - 3:00).

I took the challenge of winning SAFF: BFF suddenly sacked Fabio Lopez yesterday and took a local coach, and that coach is Maruful Haque; starting coaching at the top level of domestic football in 2008, he got the national team's responsibility for the first time, and for now, the tenure is only until next month's SAFF football, which the new coach is calling a big challenge; you used to talk as a club coach all the time, and now you are talking as the national team's coach — what is the difference; Maruful Haque: the difference is a lot, as a club is a limited circle, where you have to think only about the club, but sitting in the national team's chair, you have to keep the whole country in mind, and the responsibility of keeping the country's honour falls on your shoulders; when you stepped into the top level as Mohammedan's coach in 2008, when did you think you were ready to get the national team's responsibility; Maruf: for a few years, I had been dreaming of becoming the national team's coach, and finally, it was fulfilled; before this, I did not get any national team's responsibility at any level, but still, without losing hope, I prepared myself, but before taking Zoran Georgevic for the national team's coach, I was offered, and for whatever reason, it didn't happen, and after that, there were talks with the federation one or two more times; when exactly did the discussion with BFF about this responsibility happen; Maruf: there was talk for six-seven days, and I had a hint that something like this might happen, but I learned the final news a little while ago from the media, and everyone is congratulating and interviewing, and it's a busy time for me; the responsibility given to you must surely be a very big challenge; Maruf: of course, a big challenge, as it takes at least six weeks to make a team, and I am not even getting four weeks, but still, I have the strength of mind that I can, and I have to be able to, because from outside, many were telling the federation to give responsibility to a local this time, and many believe locals will do well, and from that side too, this is a big challenge for me; but the Bangladesh coach's chair has become even hotter than before, and the federation wants success, and if you don't become champion at SAFF, you may also be called a failure; Maruf: I know about SAFF, and in this tournament, the Bangladesh team goes to become champion every time, and I will also go to become champion; my advantage in this case is that I know the players, and I have an idea about each player, and the players also know my coaching method, what I want, and taking advantage of this, I took the challenge of winning SAFF; you surely know the reason Lopez was sacked — how was Lopez's team management in your eyes; Maruf: I haven't seen any of his practice sessions, and I haven't had any talks, but from what I understood from outside, he did excessive experiments in the team, and at this stage, there is no scope for experiments, and if you bring a forward to left-back and play him, it can have a bad effect on the team, and the players didn't even know whose position was what, which broke their morale, and there was no proper coordination in the team either, and I think these things harmed the team; we have seen you as a club coach; will we see you in a different form as the national team's coach; Maruf: to take the national team forward, I will use all my working methods and thoughts, and I will pour in the coaching knowledge I have acquired over so many days, and recently, I did the UEFA 'A' licence, and I think these will help me, and I hope I will definitely be able to show the countrymen something new; — Prothom Alo.

Franchise football with a 100-crore taka budget in 5 years: Kazi Salahuddin was coming out of the house every now and then and peeking outside, waiting for Bhaswar Goswami, executive director of the Indian institution Celebrity Management Group (CMG); with a luggage in hand, Bhaswar went straight from the airport to the BFF president's residence in Gulshan yesterday afternoon, where Chittagong Abahani's football committee chairman and Saif Powertec's chief Tarafdar Ruhul Amin was already there; after a half-hour meeting of Bhaswar Goswami and Kazi Salahuddin with him, a big announcement came: a franchise football event is being held in Bangladesh, and the Bangladesh Super League will be much like the Indian Super League (ISL); the budget for the next five tournaments has been set at 100 crore taka, and it may start by next November, while BFF will inform in detail about this within a month; the UK-based institution UK Soccer League was trying to buy the rights of Bangladesh's Premier Football League, and before that, CMG had brought a proposal to start a franchise league in Bangladesh last year, but they could not move the plan forward alone, and now, after getting partners, the initiative gained momentum; the BFF president said the franchise football will be jointly organised by the UK Soccer League, Saif Powertec, CMG and BFF, and there will be eight region-based teams in Dhaka and outside Dhaka, and besides Dhaka, matches will be held in Sylhet, Chittagong and Rajshahi, while the organisers are thinking of increasing the venues; earlier, CMG official Bhaswar had said Maradona has been attached to the BSL, and the Argentine legend will be the tournament's chairman, and yesterday too, he said the same thing, 'Maradona is still with us, and we also have written permission that he will come here'; not only that, Bhaswar also said about the plan to make the world's big clubs partners of the franchise, 'At least five clubs in Europe and Latin America have given assurance of becoming partners; in this list are France's Olympique Lyon, Argentina's Boca Juniors, Brazil's Flamengo, Uruguay's Nacional Club'; he proposed organising the league last year, but why couldn't he move forward after that; Bhaswar brought forward some problems, 'It was not possible for us alone only from India; I had informed BFF about the matter, and now we are happy that the Bangladesh federation has found some partners'; Salahuddin is also happy, 'We had been hoping for something like this for many days; today we reached a decision'; this league will become a part of BFF's calendar this time, and the Super Cup is therefore being cut from the calendar, although it was in the calendar, in recent years the tournament has gone into cold storage.

In the 4th day's matches of the CJKC-CDFA Banoful Third Division Football League, Boalkhali Upazila Sports Association, Star Club, Chittagong Royal Club and Shatabdi Gosthi got full points; yesterday, in the morning match held at the Shaheed Engineer Shamsuzzaman Bandar Stadium, Royal Club defeated Crescent Club 2-0, and Boalkhali Upazila Sports Association defeated Panchlaish Jubo Sangha 3-0; Royal Club's Shahadat alone scored both goals; Boalkhali Upazila Sports Association's Farhad scored 2 and Sabbir 1 goal; meanwhile, in the afternoon, Star Club beat Muktijoddha Sangsad Krira Chakra Lal by Jafran Chowdhury's only goal; in the evening match, Shatabdi Gosthi won 2-0 against Gosaildanga Jubo Gosthi; Shatabdi's Razzak and Lokman scored 1 goal each.

Bangladesh beat Chinese Super League club Hebei Zhongji FC by 1-0; Toklis Ahmed was the scorer; till now in this tournament, Mamun, Jibon and Toklis scored for Bangladesh; positive news is that forwards are getting a few goals; good luck Maruf, with this 'broken' team.

Ali Ashfaq plays an attacking role, most often playing as a striker; he is frequently cited as South Asia's best attacking player, and he is known for his dribbling ability, agility, speed, on-ball skills and as a free-kick specialist; he is also famous for beating players and rounding off goalkeepers; SAFF Championship history: he scored 2 goals on his first appearance in the SAFF Championship 2005, but Maldives were knocked out of the tournament in the semi-finals by India; SAFF Championship 2008: Maldives won their first ever SAFF Championship beating India in the finals, and despite Ashfaq's goalless run throughout the tournament, he assisted 6 goals for the side and was the Most Valuable Player of the tournament, and as a result, he was included in the list of goal.com's Asia's top ten performers of 2008; 2009 SAFF Championship: he became the captain and scored 3 goals for the team and was the runner-up to Most Valuable Player of the tournament but was voted the best player of the tournament by Bangladeshi media; 2011 SAFF Championship: Maldives were knocked out by India in the semi-finals by 3-1, and Ashfaq was included in the 'Eastern promise: Ten to watch in 2012' shortlist by John Duerden of espnstar.com; 2013 SAFF Championship: he scored 6 goals against Sri Lanka in the group stage, beating Lionel Messi's record of scoring 5 goals in a continental tournament match, and moreover, Ashfaq set himself another record by being the all-time top scorer of the SAFF Championship with 18 goals in total; he continued his fantastic form and scored 4 in the 8-2 thumping of Bhutan; with this he has 18 goals in the SAFF Championship; post credit: SAFF Suzuki Cup official Facebook page.

Today, the SAFF Suzuki Cup's official page posted about Ali Ashfaq; he broke the most number of goals world record at a continental tournament group stage by scoring 6 goals, previously which record was held by Lionel Messi; when the poster sees Ashfaq, it makes him remember Enamul Haque; aha, 2009 SAFF, Enamul Haque scored the most number of goals in that tournament alongside Ali Ashfaq; we were debating between us who is the best striker of South Asia, Ali Ashfaq or Enamul Haque; huh, those days.

This is the result of our 10 SAFF championships: 1 time champion, 2 times runners-up, and 2 times in the semis; in the last 2 SAFFs, they couldn't cross the group stage; with this equation, the new Bengal boss Maruf has to go down with his team.
Thank you Fabio Lopez; at least you tried your best and tried for some effective changes; good luck for your next journey.

An unfortunate loss for Chittagong City United (Noapara Lions) Club; in the Chittagong 3rd division football league, today at the Bandar Stadium, Chittagong City United (Noapara Lions) Club lost 1-0 to Shahid Shahjahan Sangha; Shahjahan Sangha scored this goal from a penalty at the end of the first half; the post and the goalkeeper stopped 2 sure goals of Chittagong City United (Noapara Lions) Club.
Rony from Bangladesh.

In the Bangladesh Championship League, some bank or insurance company is sponsoring the Bangladesh Police team for 50 lakh taka, and today they unveiled the team's jersey in a fairly grand manner; and where are our professional league teams?
Remember that goal from Atiqur Rahman Mesho; 82 minutes, Bangladesh 1-0 India.
Abdul Baten Komol, that time the fire man; remember that moment when we last met neighbour Burma; Bangladesh 2-0 Myanmar.
35-metre long ranger from Mamun; Asian Games, Bangladesh 1-0 Afghanistan.

Best goal-scoring defender Atiqur Rahman Mesho, about to cry after scoring for his national team; Bangladesh was saying, 'Take a bow, young lad; you did it'; that amazing moment you make the whole nation feel proud, and he has all the right to be emotional.
When Bangladesh gets Pakistan in football, they culturally smash them brutally; 2014 World Cup qualifiers, Bangladesh 3-0 Pakistan (Emily, Jahid and Mithun scored for Bangladesh).
Shhhhh; don't talk; it's Hemonto Vincent, who scored with a volley against Sri Lanka; he was like, 'You mad, bro; stop criticising our national team'.

Guess who is that flying man; didn't get it, right; haha, that's our captain Mamunul Islam Mamun; the best celebration the poster saw by a Bangladeshi player, 4-5 flying somersaults; full time: Bangladesh 3-0 Macao.

It's ZH7; celebration time; two goals were scored by this man; not only the Macao defender and goalkeeper but also the whole stadium was surprised watching such beauty; both goals came from long rangers, from 35 metres and 25 metres he took shots; bullet; goal; oh god, it's ZH7, an artist of the beautiful game of football.

Maruful Haque has already started analysis of SAFF's opponents, saying if the Afghanistan team from the World Cup qualifiers plays at SAFF, it's possible to beat them; he wants to select the team in each match according to the opponent's weakness and strength; the primary target is the semi-final; today, BFF will give Maruful Haque a 50-man preliminary player list; Maruful Haque wants to start training with 25/30 players; there has been an indication that Zahid Hasan Emily is returning to the team again — Daily Star.
Look at that gallery; they are waving; Sabuj is the man who made 30 thousand crowd cheering; 2010 SA Games semi-final, full time: Bangladesh 1-0 India.

AFC Aspiring MA of the Year 2015: Bangladesh; the Bangladesh Football Federation has been adjudged the AFC Aspiring Member Association of the Year at the AFC Annual Awards 2015 celebration held in the Indian capital city of New Delhi on Sunday evening; the prestigious award is given to a Member Association in recognition of its professional administration and governance as well as its exceptional contribution to the development and promotion of the game at all levels within the country; recognising the diversity of MAs in terms of facilities and resources and looking to ensure that more nations will receive recognition for their efforts and achievements in developing football in their country, the AFC in 2013 introduced three winners for the Member Association of the Year award as opposed to just one; the AFC's 46 Member Associations are divided into three categories namely 'Inspiring', 'Developing' and 'Aspiring' based on their overall footballing prowess; Member Associations are assessed and awarded points on various areas encompassing the association's activities such as the organisation of courses and seminars, competitions, grassroots and youth development, women's programmes, social responsibility and special projects; points are also given for an MA's hosting of AFC qualifying and finals tournaments as well as their national and club teams' placing in AFC and FIFA competitions throughout the year.

Post asking if anyone is near Asian University; not about football.

Meme-style post: Bangladesh fans say 'we can also do it', while Bangladeshi clubs apologise.

Off-topic post asking who is from Chittagong City and to inbox the poster.

Page promotion post asking people to like the page and stay with them.

Post containing only an emoticon.

Fan wishes the Bangladesh national football team the best of luck.

Fan says they lost and tries to stay positive, but cannot anymore, and says the federation and team do not even deserve criticism.

Short post saying there is nothing more to say.

Short post saying 'Lopez strikes once more'.

Prothom Alo report on the chaos at the team hotel after the semi-final defeat, as club officials fought over the players.

Sarcastic post claiming 'Yes we won the Bangabandhu Gold Cup', thanking Bangladesh for the support.

posts.summary: Introduces Zidan Mia, a 14-year-old of Bangladeshi origin recognised at the Asian Football Awards, who has played in the UK for three years.

Poster says despite the Gold Cup failure, one improvement was visible: no stamina shortage, the players had the breath to play at this level.

Fan asks who the Olympic team coach is and who announced the team, questioning why Mamunul is not among the three seniors (Jamal, Reza and Jibon) and calling Jibon and Sajib big miss-masters.

Notes the 2026 World Cup will have 48 teams, giving Bangladesh better chances, and asks whether they will be ready by then.
Post containing only an emoticon.
Eid Mubarak wishes to all group members.
Short post reading 'The debate is back on'.

Questions whether Bangladesh's failure is really due to poor players, arguing the real causes are lack of willpower and frequent coach changes, and hopes Jamie Day gets time to do well at the SAFF.

Lamests that if the Bangabandhu Gold Cup were held now, Bangladesh could have played against those teams.

Post containing only the word 'undefined' followed by emojis.
Post containing only the word 'undefined' followed by emojis.

Questions why football development should rely only on corporates, noting Real Kashmir FC will play the I-League within three years of founding, while Sylhet supplies many players but has no team of its own and Beanibazar's side is now Dhaka United.
Jokes about the Bangladesh football team's new signing.
Asks whether anyone knows about the player in the picture.

Urges bidding corruption farewell, taking proper plans, spreading football beyond Dhaka across the whole country, and nurturing youth footballers so Bangladesh can play before 2050.

Mocks that SAFF is actually run by BFF, Helal and Shohag, after Changlimithang Stadium was rendered as 'Chalimithang Stadium', noting a defamation case could be filed if Bangabandhu Stadium's name were distorted like that.
Short post calling Bengalis a football-crazy nation.
Tells Kazi Salahuddin to step down with honour, saying he has eaten up the country's football and that the Bangladesh team practising in Colombia's jersey is a shame for the whole country.
Shares a Pavilion article comparing Belgium's FA, which walked the opposite path by not recalling players for results, with Bangladesh.

Questions why football means only Brazil-Argentina, Messi, Neymar or Ronaldo, and why district-league banners carry their photos when Bangladesh has its own footballers.

Sardonically lists some of Kazi Salahuddin's successes: keeping the Premier League running, keeping the girls' age-group team in residential camp, starting age-group tournaments as SAFF president, and starting FIFA-window friendlies, asking if there is anything else.

Addresses Jafar Iqbal as a big fan, praising players like him for keeping Bangladesh football's dying dream alive, but scolding him for being awake at 11:40 pm in the Qatar camp and urging him to be professional.

Wishes a happy birthday to Fuad Hasan Ether, the youngest member of the group's admin panel.
Hashtag post demanding Salahuddin's removal and calling to save Bangladesh football and BFF, and for the golden past to return.
Sarcastically asks whether today's World Cup final tickets can be got from BFF through the black-market syndicate.

Reports India's main team is not coming to the SAFF Cup, publishing the Indian coach's squad with all senior players left out.
Notes France won the World Cup without a number nine and asks whether Bangladesh cannot win the SAFF.

Satirical post hoping Brazil and Argentina send free visas to Bangladeshi supporters and stand by the parents of the three children who died, lamenting that Bangladeshis have no joy of their own and celebrate others' victories.

Praises Samad Yousuf as one of the best defenders in the Bangladesh Premier League and the living legend of Dhaka Abahani, pictured with the league title.

Long rant giving up hope on a system run by corrupt people, calling BFF officials thieves who make the team practise in another country's jersey, then praising group members like Arefin who finds streaming links and Lincoln who plans to build an academy.

Asks for prayers and cooperation while trying to help the country's football and its talented players.
Shares the BFF XI team photo from yesterday's practice match against Al Mesaimeer SC in Qatar.
Jokes that Bangladesh can destroy Argentina in kabaddi and cricket, and with Argentina's current defence probably beat them in football too, sharing a YouTube link.
Mourns fifth-grader Siam, a lively boy who dreamt of becoming a big footballer, killed by a speeding microbus on his way home from school.
Reports that due to the organisers' mistake the names of the UAE and Palestine were left out, so the 2018 Asian Games grouping will be done afresh.

Short post reading 'freestyling' with a thinking emoji.

Reports 18-year-old Gambian forward Sainey Bojang is on trial at Sheikh Jamal, having last played for AS Douanes in the Senegal Premier League.
