Asks where the BFF official jersey can be found and what it costs.
Complaint that the offer made to play for them was basically peanuts.

Pushes back against BFF's former stars who mocked the team for not reaching the semi-final, noting the Maldives once beaten 8-0 by Bangladesh are now champions, and asks how many academies the critics have given the country.
Congratulates Maldives on winning the SAFF Cup as a deserving team, saying rankings are only numbers and that courage and determination to win bring success.
Cricket post about Tamim Iqbal batting one-handed with a cracked finger against Sri Lanka in the Asia Cup, framing it as national-team spirit and saying it is not off-topic.

Reports goalkeeper Nurul Karim from Chittagong has signed for Nepal A Division side Friends Club, having earlier played nine straight matches for Sankata Boys Club in 2010 before injury struck; despite playing for Bangladesh's U-14 to U-21 teams he never got a senior-team chance, and he still dreams of wearing the Bangladesh jersey.
Goal! Bangladesh have gone ahead against Bahrain in the AFC U-16 Championship qualifying match.

Corrects earlier wrong information: Mohammedan's new coach is not former Celtic assistant John Collins, a Scot, but an English coach named Christopher Evans, apologising for posting unconfirmed media reports at noon.
Shares a photo of Bashundhara Kings' home ground, calling it one of the best football fields in the country.
Thanks the group for accepting the request and sends greetings from Kolkata, saying as an East Bengal supporter he likes Bangladesh football equally.
Shares the first Mohammedan jersey in his domestic club jersey collection, thanking Abid for it, and says he intends to keep at least one jersey from every club, hoping players will help.
Breaking news citing Prothom Alo: SAFF-playing goalkeeper Sohel did not get a place in Bangladesh's Bangabandhu Gold Cup squad.

Sarcastic post claiming goalkeeper Sohel, who played brilliantly in the SAFF, has been dropped from the Gold Cup, blaming him for Bangladesh's group-stage exit and mocking those who picked him in the team.

Contrasts cricketer Tamim Iqbal being rewarded 10 lakh taka by Amber Group for batting one-handed against Sri Lanka with the U-15 and U-16 girls who keep bringing success, even reaching Asia's top eight last year, yet get only a little money and a crest, with no academy and no sponsor, asking whether they will ever get the fruit of their labour.
Post celebrating Saad Uddin and Biplu Ahmed, who represented Bangladesh in the Asian Games and SAFF football.
Reports Sheikh Russel's third signing this season is Brazilian forward Alex Rafael, last with Vietnam top-tier side Nam Dinh.
Post listing Japan, Australia and England with a smiley.
Asks to know the foreign player collections of Sheikh Jamal and Dhaka Abahani.
Reports the Bangladesh women's U-16 team lead Lebanon 5-0 at the end of the first half.
Reports the Bangladesh women's U-16 team beat Lebanon U-16 8-0 at full time, after putting ten past Bahrain in the previous match, congratulating Bangladesh.
Jokingly calls the Bangladesh women's U-16 team's goalkeeper the poor man's Manuel Neuer.
Asks if anyone from Nilphamari is in the group, saying they are leaving tomorrow for Nilphamari to watch the Bashundhara Kings match.
Notes the Vietnam versus Bahrain women's U-16 match is on, with Vietnam leading 10-0 at the end of the first half, so Bangladesh's real test will be against Vietnam.

Transfer update: Saif's fourth and final signing this season is Russian midfielder Denis Bolshakov, last with Russia's third-division FSK Dolgoprudny, who played for Nice's B team in 2004-05 and eight matches for Russia U-19 and U-17; Saif had earlier signed Deiner Cordoba, Jhonattan Cordoba and Korean Park.
Lists tomorrow's fixtures for 21 September: a pre-season friendly between Bashundhara Kings and New Radiant, and the Bodousa Cup semi-final between Gokulam Kerala FC and Saif SC.
Transfer update: Nigerian striker Matthew Chinedu signed by Arambagh KS for the upcoming season, having scored six goals in 20 matches for Farashganj SC last season.
Cannot understand Bangladesh's FIFA ranking: after a good SAFF they expected to climb from 194 to 170-179, having beaten 183rd-ranked Bhutan by two goals, but they moved up only one place to 193.
Notes the Bashundhara Kings versus New Radiant international club friendly match is about to start, with good wishes from Bashundhara Kings Fans Gopalganj.
Announces the FIFA International Club Friendly between Bashundhara Kings and New Radiant SC of the Maldives, kicking off at 3:30pm live on DESH TV, with live score links.
Self-deprecating post saying that after so many years he got no recognition for inventing the mid-match interview and news broadcasting.
Asks who scored for Bashundhara Kings and Saif.
Asks when the Bangladesh versus Vietnam match in the U-16 women's AFC qualifiers will start.

Reports a football-filled day: Bangladesh U-16 women beat UAE U-16 7-0, Bashundhara Kings beat New Radiant 4-1 and Saif Sporting beat Kerala FC 1-0, and describes the group's delegation at Nilphamari watching Bashundhara Kings play skilful football in front of 20,000-plus fans, thanking club president Imrul Hassan.
Asks Bashundhara Kings for some exciting match photos.
Notes that after losing nine matches in a row against Maldives sides over the last 15 years, finally a different result came, and wonderfully so.
Gives the Bangabandhu Gold Cup 2018 fixtures, running 1-12 October at 6:30pm, with Group A of Bangladesh, Laos and Philippines and Group B of Nepal, Palestine and Tajikistan.

Transfer update on Ctg Abahani's foreign players: Nigerian striker Magalan Awala, who scored six goals in ten matches for Muktijoddha last season; Gambian Mamadou Bah, who scored four in his first six matches for Sheikh Jamal before losing his place; and Nigerian defender Mufta Lawal, staying at Chittagong Abahani.
Notes the Mexican striker is the only topic of discussion everywhere now, in America, Poland and Mexico: only Quess East Bengal FC.
Notes the U-16 women's footballers have worked hard for tomorrow's big match against Vietnam.
Complains someone is deliberately ruining Bashundhara Kings' wiki page again and again, having deleted a lot of it again three hours ago.
Shares Costa Rican media coverage after the Bashundhara Kings versus NRSC match, noting a Costa Rican commented on Bashundhara's official page that he wants to buy a Bashundhara Kings jersey.
Asks whether this is the official page and says it will be verified, urging everyone to follow it.
Mocks the Dhaka Abahani page, asking whether it is the page the club deserves and saying the officials at least deserve it.

Shares a Janakantha online piece written after a funny experience in Nilphamari, joking that if the public realised they are not footballers they would be disappointed and give them a mass beating after pulling them off the bus.
Claims that in Bangladesh, getting your name in BFF means an expanded opportunity to do business and politics, sharing an AFC article on Thailand's transformation from regional to continental giants.
Asks how many teams from Bangladesh will play in the 2019 AFC Cup, and whether one team will take part in the playoffs or from the group stage if the 2018-19 BPL does not finish before the AFC Cup.
Notes the unwritten final between Bangladesh and Vietnam in the U-16 women's football is starting now, live on BTV World.
Suggests it would be great if Bashundhara Kings could arrange a match with India's East Bengal, since both teams have built very strong squads this season and such a match would excite spectators.

Breaking news: Saif Sporting Club clinched the Bodousa Cup title, a FIFA tier-2 club competition organised by Assam FA and AIFF, with a 2-0 win over ISL side Jamshedpur FC Reserves in the final at Katchujan Field, Tinsukia.
Reports the Bangladesh U-16 women's team reached the main qualifying round of the AFC U-16 Championship by beating Vietnam U-16 2-0, congratulating Bangladesh.
Reports Saif Sporting Club are champions of the 10th Bodousa Cup tournament in Assam, India.
Notes Shahed was player of the tournament of the 2018 Bodousa Cup.
Post with the hashtag SportsManship.
Says if the league had started right after the SAFF, two AFC Cup slots could have been got.
Notes that according to the Daily Star, Bangladesh is going to get only one slot in the AFC Cup, and that too only a qualifier slot as Fed Cup champions.
Asks Arefin Zeesan, as someone relatively new to Bangladesh club football, whether Abahani and Mohammedan are in the same league as Bashundhara Kings and how many leagues there are in Bangladesh.

Argues the women's team, which is going step by step toward success, needs more protection, asking why there is a male manager in the women's team and why technical director Paul Smalley is always with the women's team, and demanding 100 percent security for the players.
Asks who the other three confirmed foreigners of Bashundhara Kings are for the 2018-19 season.
Post containing only a sceptical emoticon.
Says if the national teams come it will be great.
Asks when the league will start.

entities.name: Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman National Gold Cup

posts.summary: Criticises the lack of promotion of the Bangabandhu Gold Cup 2018 in Sylhet, supposedly because the U-17 National Gold Cup is running at the same time and spectators would be confused, and mocks holding tournaments in the names of the Father of the Nation and Sheikh Kamal for money.
Asks whether there is any Mohammedan supporter in group A.
Notes Palestine are the highest-ranked team, sitting 100th in FIFA's world rankings, followed by the next team.
Reports the new Mexican striker Enrique has arrived at Kolkata airport for Quess East Bengal FC, calling him the most valuable player in I-League history.
Notes the Bangladesh women's U-18 football team is now at Bhutan airport.

Transfer update on Rahmatganj MFS's foreign players: Congolese striker Siyo Zunapio returning from Churchill Brothers after 10 goals in 20 matches for Brothers, Nigerian defender Monday Osagie returning from Churchill Brothers, and Nigerian defensive midfielder Dami Emmanuel returning to domestic football.
Asks about Dhaka Abahani's foreign signings.
Reports strikers Matin Mia and Jafar Iqbal have returned to the Bangladesh team, while Saad Uddin and Shakhawat Hossain Roni have been dropped.
Reports Saad Uddin came to Sylhet on holiday after the SAFF Championship and was injured in a road accident, so coach Jamie Day dropped him from the team, while others were dropped for lack of form.
Calls it a very sad incident and hopes he recovers quickly and returns to the field.
Post claiming one solution for football development is a rally.
Asks whether anyone can give a picture or video of Cox's Bazar stadium.

Reports Bangladesh are hopeful in Bhutan for the women's SAFF U-18 tournament starting Friday, in Group B with Nepal and Pakistan, opening against Pakistan on 30 September at Changlimithang Stadium, with coach Golam Rabbani Choton saying they will play for the title.
Recalls the golden time of black and white, Mohammedan, hoping it will return in its former form with changing times.
Asks why Bangladeshi clubs are so indifferent about websites, noting Mohammedan's was only in name, Bashundhara Kings' is not up to standard, and new club Saif Sporting have no website at all.
Reports every Gold Cup match will be broadcast by three Bangladeshi channels, BTV, Maasranga Television and Nagorik TV, plus Radio Bhumi 92.8 FM, wishing the Bangladesh football team well.

Asks whether Wikipedia is right that Saif Sporting's current squad includes Russian international Denis Glushakov, who played for Russia U-21 and 57 times for the Russia national team including the Euros, or whether it is wrong information.
Reports the Bangladesh national football team has reached Sylhet to play the Bangabandhu International Gold Cup Football Tournament, as the first team in the six-nation tournament.
Birthday wishes to sports-loving Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on behalf of the national women's football team.

Notes several group admins are going from Dhaka to Sylhet tomorrow to watch the Bangabandhu Gold Cup match Bangladesh versus Laos, inviting anyone who wants to come along or watch together to contact them.
Reports Saad Uddin has been ruled out of the Bangabandhu Gold Cup after being injured in a road accident.
Asks whether everyone is officially sending national teams to the Gold Cup.
Asks about the Laos national football team: how their players fare globally, what their style of play is, and who their best star is.

Recalls the last of the previous three Sylhet events was not pleasant: in the SAFF U-16 final on 18 August 2015 between Bangladesh and India, the stadium floodlights suddenly went off midway through the game, panicking spectators and worrying the Indian team and foreign officials.

Summarises the Gold Cup teams' strength: Nepal, Laos and Tajikistan full-strength, Philippines second-string with the first squad going to Oman, and Palestine second-string claiming the matches are unofficial, though FIFA's website lists official recognition.

Reports Japanese player Atsushi Yonezawa has come to Dhaka to play for Rahmatganj MFS in the Asian quota, having won the last two I-Leagues with two different clubs, Aizawl in 2016-17 and Minerva Punjab in 2017-18.
Notes that although this is news of a foreign club, Bangladeshi clubs can learn from it: bringing up new talent and signing long-term contracts with them will benefit them in the end.

Muses that a decade and a half of dreaming about Bangladesh football could fill a trilogy film centred on a character inspired by Mashrafe, but only if the Nolan brothers and Hans Zimmer or A.R. Rahman make it, since Bangladesh football will not reach anywhere before doomsday.

Gives Bangladesh's possible group on the way to the main round of the AFC U16 Women's Championship, from which the two semi-finalists will qualify: China or Australia, Bangladesh, Laos or Iran, and Vietnam or Philippines.
Recalls Matin's superhuman goal against Muktijoddha last season in the BPL, taking the ball from his own defence and beating four opposition players, noting it could not become the world's best goal.

Reports Costa Rican vice-captain Daniel Colindres earns about 2 lakh 30 thousand taka a day, and criticises Bashundhara Kings' next three signings as ISL reject Belfort, I-League reject Saighani and Maldives league reject Gotor, calling them disappointing after bringing in an active World Cupper.

Quotes a coach saying they want to forget what happened at the SAFF, that this is a new tournament and the boys will do well with Matin and Sufil taking responsibility, and that having a local coach in the Bangladesh team is no problem.
Notes Bangladesh scored two fours, eight goals, against Pakistan in the first half of the match in Bhutan on Sunday.

Asks what benefit playing the 2018 Gold Cup brings, noting the player who captained the 2017 Bangabandhu Gold Cup runners-up and was man of the tournament, receiving his award from the Prime Minister, is today a van driver while still a class six student.
Quotes a visiting team saying their main team has not come and they have brought a second-string team.

Reports Bangladesh thrashed Pakistan 17-0 in the women's U-18 SAFF Championship to reach the semi-final, recalling the 14-0 win over Pakistan in the SAFF U-15 last August and noting Nepal beat Pakistan 12-0 on the first day.
Notes Sylhet boys Matin Mia and Mahbubur Rahman are the strikers, with coach Jamie Day seeing Sylhet's 'khep master' Matin as the team's number one striker and saying expectations of him are high.
Congratulates Tajikistan on qualifying for the U-17 World Cup for the second time by beating North Korea, despite losing 6-2 to Malaysia in the first match of the first round.

Previews the Bangabandhu Gold Cup starting tomorrow at Sylhet District Stadium with Bangladesh against Laos, noting the team visited Hazrat Shah Jalal's shrine and practised at Sylhet BKSP, and lists the 23-man Bangladesh squad.
Reports Saif Sporting beat ATK Reserves 3-0, with Jhonattan scoring twice and Shadhin once, praising Saif's good performance.

Notes Bangladesh will play on the field and Bangladesh Football - Walking Around The Dreams will be in the gallery, with three group admins now in Sylhet to enjoy the Bangabandhu Gold Cup match against Laos.
Notes that forgetting the SAFF failure, Bangladesh wants to turn around and make the Gold Cup title their own, with all players needing to play their best.
Shares a post giving the details of the Bangabandhu Gold Cup 2018 at a glance.
Asks whether the Bangladesh women's U19 team will take part in the AFC U19 qualifier.
Invites fans to watch today's Bangladesh versus Laos match live together in the field with the SSSA - Orange Tigers team, giving contact numbers.
Echoes Jitu and Lincoln's call for a full-fledged Bangabandhu football academy, arguing many use the name for business more than good work, and his demand is selfless, for the country's honour.

Match thread for the 2018 Bangabandhu Gold Cup match day one, Bangladesh versus Laos at 6:30pm at Sylhet District Stadium, live on BTV, Maasranga TV and Nagorik TV, asking all match comments be posted here.
Lists the final eleven: Ashraful Rana, Bishwanath, Badsha, Topu Barman, Wali Faisal, Jamal Bhuiyan, Biplu, Johnny, Robiul, Sufil and Jibon.
Notes Bangladesh could not do it in the SAFF Championship at home and were eliminated from the semi-final, and now want to turn around in the Bangabandhu Gold Cup at home.
Asks what the logic is in not keeping Yasin Khan, one of South Asia's best centre-backs, in the main eleven, as he is on the bench again today.
Reports Bangladesh went ahead against Laos in the 14th minute of the second half, with Jibon entering the box and Biplu scoring on his second attempt from Jibon's pass.
Congratulates the Bangladesh team and Biplu.
Reports hosts Bangladesh made an auspicious start to the Bangabandhu Gold Cup by beating Laos with Biplu Ahmed's only goal in the 61st minute, noting the lack of a perfect finisher.

Detailed analysis of the Laos win, arguing 1-0 could easily have been 4-0, praising Topu as man of the match and Wali's fitness and corners, and criticising Bishwanath and Badsha's line maintenance and Jafar's sluggishness.

Notes Biplu debuted internationally against Sri Lanka, played three matches in SAFF and one in the Bangabandhu Gold Cup, and scored his first international goal in a five-match career, on home ground.
Reports that immediately after the goal Biplu ran to the gallery near the south-west corner and saluted someone, and after the match he revealed the secret of that salute.
Says the match, broadcasting and commentary were all great.
Reports the fifth edition of the Bangabandhu International Gold Cup was inaugurated at Sylhet District Stadium on Monday at 6pm, with Bangladesh and Laos taking the field at 6:33pm.
Says sports are mixed in the blood of Sylhetis, sharing a Facebook post.
Asks which teams are participating in this year's Bangabandhu Gold Cup, having heard Palestine is in it.
Reports the Gold Cup teams have to practise on a single ground because the organisers are not getting the BGB ground, whose authorities are not letting anyone enter.

Profiles goalkeeper Shahidul Yusuf Sohel as extraordinary in positioning, vision, anticipation and reflexes, but argues his weakness in flight and nerves cost him the regular number one spot despite his penalty-saving talent.

Analyses Bangladesh's 4-4-2 formation against Laos, praising the wing build-up and Robiul and Biplu, suggesting Jafar should get Sufil's free role, and comparing the Jibon-Sufil combination to France's Giroud and Griezmann.
Says it is good to see LED displays on the Gold Cup sidelines this year and asks when the Bangladesh Premier League will do that, as the league needs to be reinvented technology-wise.
Notes Bimal Magar, who scored two goals, is not in Nepal's Bangabandhu Gold Cup team, and Nepal has not brought a midfielder like Rohit Chand either.
Jokes that after Brazil and Argentina, now FC Barcelona are training at Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club's ground, tagging it as all rumours.
Notes that after the news, the team could not be organised that way, with some of the best players missing from the team.
Asks for the heights of the three tallest players in the Bangladesh team, goalkeeper not included, saying he cannot find them.

Recounts Biplu's story of being fast-tracked at the Agargaon passport office after the officer explained he is a footballer representing the country, showing him the pride of representing the country.
Asks how Rana, the national team's main goalkeeper in the Bangabandhu Gold Cup, is taking Bangladesh's SAFF collapse due to Shahidul Alam Sohel's mistake.
Reports Biplu scored his first international goal at Sylhet District Stadium, where his childhood was spent and his football schooling began, and spoke with SNP Sports about his upbringing.
Notes Laos take the field today in their last match of the Bangabandhu Gold Cup, starting at 6:30pm at Sylhet District Stadium.
Duplicate report of the pre-season friendly: Saif SC 2-0 Kolkata Mohammedan, with goals from Cordoba and Dennis, and clean sheets in all five games.
Reports a pre-season friendly: Saif SC 2-0 Kolkata Mohammedan, with goals from Cordoba and Dennis, and clean sheets in all five games.
Asks whether anyone knows when Federation Cup 2018 will start.
Notes there were three penalties in one match, two of them in favour of one team, and argues if the penalties result in goals no team should be deprived of victory.
Recalls a past match where Bangladesh fell behind 2-0 in the first half, drew 2-2 in the second, then conceded a goal near the final whistle, leaving the players with the pain of shattered dreams.
Asks when transfers will start, noting they will end on the 10th.
Reports the Philippines' captain threatened Bangladesh ahead of their match.
Notes the Philippines were in the advantageous position while Laos had no alternative but to win, and Laos could not overcome the pressure of the international tournament.

Notes BFF's confirmed income from the ongoing Bangabandhu Gold Cup is one crore taka, with K-Sports already paying 50 lakh and ticket money also going to BFF, and asks why BFF neglects the footballers' minimum demand of new jerseys.

Analyses the Philippines' attacks against Laos, 42 percent from the left flank, 32 percent through midfield and 26 percent from the right, arguing Sufil and Biplu can hurt their defence if the forwards are blocked.
A quote from an unnamed player saying his job is to handle the defence first and go up later, mentioning free-kicks and corner kicks.
A post consisting only of a clapping emoji.
Asks whether there will be a game against the Philippines ahead.
Reports Jamal saying Bangladesh, having confirmed the semi-final, still want victory against whichever team, as they play to win.

Revises his prediction on Palestine's Gold Cup squad, explaining which foreign-based players are missing outside the FIFA window and who returned, and now puts Palestine and Tajikistan in the same row as favourites.
Notes the favourite team's match falls on a holiday, so spectators will be many, but a flood of spectators does not mean pressure, as coach Jamie Day finds inspiration in their presence.
Notes Palestine took the field for the first time in the Bangabandhu International Gold Cup football tournament.
Reports Sheikh Russel KC are signing Australian striker Dumba Naki in the Asian quota for the upcoming season, a 24-year-old with professional league experience in Australia.
Reports Palestine are ahead by a clear 2-0 margin as the 90 minutes end and extra time is being played.
Reports Matin Mia is eager to play against the Philippines on Friday, but coach Jamie Day is angry with 'Khep Master' Matin Mia, and his dream of playing on Friday appears over.
Notes everyone had flags in hand but they were not citizens of Palestine, as the spectators shouting for Palestine were Bangladeshi.

Notes even though the Philippines sent a second team, 19 of their 21 squad members have senior international experience, showing the depth of their pool and the Gold Cup's higher quality compared to the recent SAFF.
Notes most of the strikers in the team are from Sylhet, naming Sufil from Sreemangal, Biplu Ahmed from Bonkolapara and Matin Mia from Balaganj, ahead of Bangladesh's last group match today.

Shares Mahbubur Rahman Sufil's stats across all levels since September last year, 17 matches and 8 goals, noting after Enamul Haque he is the first to show regular goalscoring effort that even Emily could not.
Reports that despite being one of the team's best stars, Matin pleaded to play even one minute for the national team on the Sylhet ground, though he had no need to plead, and that coach Jamie Day...

Previews tonight's Bangladesh versus Philippines match, noting both teams beat Laos so both semi-finals are confirmed, and whoever loses today will face Palestine, the Gold Cup favourite, in the semi-final.
Notes the first list that reached media workers also carried the signatures of coach Jamie Day and manager Satyajit Das Rupu, as the two teams took the field and BFF's media operation began.
Says Bangladesh is playing wonderfully and even in defeat there is peace watching this game, thanking Jamie Day and saying he will change the face of the team if he stays.
Asks why there is no pressing today, the coach's instruction or Sufil's absence, suggesting it is the coach's decision and the whole team is not pressing.
Asks why he did not at least take a shot, saying a shot would easily have been a goal.
Says it was a certain penalty.
Argues players in the attacking zone do not know positioning, when to pass and when to shoot, and their heading is so poor a diagonal header is impossible.
Asks Jibon to take advice from Nakib or Aslam on how to score with the head, and from Sufil on how to increase fitness.

Reports Bangladesh lost to the Philippines in front of thousands of spectators in Sylhet, with Daniel scoring the only goal in the 22nd minute, but played improved and organised football, having rested five main players after securing the semi-final against Laos.

Notes Bangladesh lost 1-0 to the strong Philippines in the Gold Cup but will play the semi-final against Palestine, while the girls scored three goals against Bhutan in the SAFF U-18 Championship semi-final.
A post consisting only of 'The irony of fate', with no further context.

Reports Bangladesh's girls beat Bhutan 4-0 in the U-18 Women's Championship semi-final, with goals from Sanjida Akter, Mishrat Jahan Moushumi, Krishna Rani Sarkar and Shamsunnahar's penalty, reaching the final.
Says he did not like Bangladesh's play today for lack of pressing and intensity, and argues it was lucky Mamunul did not play, as his over-commanding would have spoiled everyone's game.
Profiles Spanish defender Jorge Gotor, who played against Cristiano Ronaldo and for Spain U-17, and praises Bashundhara Kings for signing him after World Cup star Daniel Colindres.
Reports hosts Bangladesh won against Laos in the first match of the Bangabandhu Gold Cup, and that Topu Barman and company face the Philippines in the second match on Friday.

Notes Bangladesh had eight shots on target to the Philippines' one, but the final score was Philippines 1-0 Bangladesh, arguing the difference was the goalkeeper and that Bangladesh needs a young, long, athletic goalkeeper.

Admits a mistake and praises coach Jamie Day as ultimately professional for changing the formation against Laos and the mode of play against the Philippines, noting Bangladesh had seven on-target shots to the Philippines' one but lost to their only chance.
Praises goal number four, a pass from outside the box with position sense.
Says even if it is not possible in real life, doing it here consoles the mind.
A vague post about who watches whose deeds and the hullabaloo of law-breaking where there is law, with no clear football context.
Describes Nepal goalkeeper Bikesh diving to save Musa's shot from a difficult angle in the 16th minute, and staying busy while Palestine's goalkeeper came up from time to time.
Reports coach Jamie Day spoke about the semi-final after the match against the Philippines, and that there was also talk about the semi-final after the Philippines' match against Laos.
Quotes Maria, Shopna and Shamsunnahar saying in one word that they will return home with the title.
Notes that around 1960 an Italian manager named Nereo took charge of Inter Milan and invented a particular formula, sharing a tactics post.
Asks where he can buy the latest 2018 home jersey of the Bangladesh national football team, authentic or genuine.
Shares a photo, probably a moment from an Abahani versus Brothers match in the 80s or 90s, praising the spot jump of the player wearing jersey number 9.
Notes Bangladesh played way better than the Philippines and beat Laos, both higher-ranked teams, and looks forward to seeing how they play against Palestine, ranked 73 in FIFA as late as March 2018.

Argues an international tournament with six countries can earn praise from foreign teams, but it is not praised if its own country's footballers are not honoured, noting former players too have bleeding pain in their hearts.
Calls on those 'deprived' who have not yet received any compensation to contact soon, with no further context.
Says love will go on and on, and not to be jealous.
Teases that Bashundhara Kings will come with some unbelievable twist again, asking fans to wait.
Reports Bangladesh became SAFF champions by beating Nepal 1-0 in Thimphu, Bhutan, with Masura Parvin scoring in the 49th minute, congratulating the Tigresses.
Notes any new women's event in SAFF means Bangladesh's girls triumphing, with the girls of Bengal raising the graph of success in age-level football.
Reports Bangladesh beat Nepal in the final of the first-ever U-18 Women's Championship in Thimphu, Bhutan, with Masura Parvin heading the only goal in the 47th minute from a set piece.
Wishes a coach a happy birthday.
A post consisting only of an annoyed emoji, with no clear context.
A post consisting only of 'Good news though', with no further context.

Reports Brazilian forward Marcos Vinicius de Costa Soares de Silva has signed for Bashundhara Kings after a season in the Thai league, with chairman Imrul Hassan waiting for his visa and arrival in Dhaka.
Asks whether we are crossing the limit of joking, arguing matches are being given on farmland unfit even for school football, and wondering how only this federation escapes a ban.

Praises Marcos Vinicius as looking like a beast on his profile, defends Bashundhara Kings against claims supporters have become too much, and hopes an Asian physical defensive midfielder completes the team.
Complains Cox's Bazar Stadium has hardly any grass, uneven soil and a muddy goalpost area, arguing international matches should not be held there.
Notes Casas, who kept brilliantly against Bangladesh, was brilliant again in this match, saving at least four certain goals before conceding one in the first half.
Suggests Bangladesh can stop Palestine by playing defensively and countering with a 5-4-1 formation, fouling in midfield and tackling their good players.

Breaking news that a trial has finally been organised for Ashaan, thanking Mohammedan FC, captain Taklis and Imrul Gazi for recommending and supporting him to break into the Bangladesh football market.
Asks how Palestine advanced so far in football when its people do not even get a chance to live properly, and asks someone to explain their method.
Congratulates Reasat on getting his UEFA B licence from the German Football Association and starting part-time work as a coach at the Llanelli AFC youth academy.
Notes Palestine are 93 places ahead of Bangladesh in the FIFA rankings, 100th against 193rd, and Bangladesh must face a tough test against them in the Bangabandhu Gold Cup.

Protests that Sirat Jahan Shopna, who scored 8 goals including a double hat-trick against Pakistan, was denied the SAFF U-18 Championship top scorer award, accusing the SAFF committee of staging drama in the final.
Says to send the tough opponent out of the tournament and play the final, Bangladesh must give their best, with the attackers catching fire and overcoming their finishing failures.
Suggests the wet field could be a good tactic to stop Palestine.
Asks what time Bangladesh's match is today.
Says since the field is muddy, the footballers should take spiked boots.

Previews the Bangabandhu Gold Cup semi-final at Cox's Bazar Stadium between Bangladesh and Palestine, ranked 194 and 100, recapping how Bangladesh reached the semi-final and noting the match will be broadcast live.
Notes Saif Sporting Club practised today at the United International University ground.
Shares a Cox's Bazar weather update showing rain likely for today's match, hoping Palestine will be beaten in the rain.
Shares Bangladesh's starting eleven in a 4-1-4-1 formation: Rana; Bishwanath, Badsha, Topu, Wali; Jamal; Masuk, Emon; Sufil, Biplu; Jibon, hoping Bangladesh will win.
Jokes that for the remaining 45 minutes, if needed let Rupu and Jamie Day play, but for God's sake substitute Jibon.
Sarcastically says the whole of Bangladesh is overwhelmed watching Jibon's play, and if Palestine wins he is the rightful man of the match.
Asks whether BFF will teach the national team to play in such fields and take them to the World Cup, or whether BFF does not even have funds to fix the field's grass.
Says they had to lose again today due to the lack of a striker.

News that a BFF Elite Academy development team will play in the next BCL, with trials for 116 players from 64 districts in January.
Fan asks why Rafael was not made captain instead, suggesting Rupu will give it to Jibon, who will return to the national team in January.
Long essay arguing the 2018 Asian Games run was built on the 2017 youth batches and academy exposure, and that domestic competition, refereeing and fixture manipulation still hold Bangladesh back.
Mannaf Rabbi's goal for Sheikh Russel against Dhaka Abahani.
Fan teases that a new joker has arrived in Bangladesh football and asks readers to guess who.
Writer defends himself against claims he never wrote in Bashundhara's favour, pointing to three pro-Bashundhara pieces in the comments.
Video of Gomez's goal against Sheikh Russel.
Fan wishes Bangladesh U19 women's star Ritu Porna Chakma a happy birthday.
BFF plans to appoint age-level coaches next year ahead of the SAFF U16 and AFC U17 championships.
Long essay arguing the subcontinent's best coaches have been English, backing Stephen Constantine for Bangladesh and Maruful Haque as the only qualified local coach needing four years.
Fan slams the poor broadcast of the Federation Cup, which carries an AFC Cup slot, and criticises quota players and the quota federation committee.
Fan looks back on 2021.
Joke post that Bishwanath Ghosh has left the chat, noting Shoaib Akhtar's fastest ball was 161.2 km/h.
Fan wishes someone a happy birthday.
Fan asks why a Finland top-tier and age-level player like Tariq must sit on the bench for a local player or play out of position.

Long essay by Miraj Mahbub arguing Abahani's Independence Cup final win over Bashundhara Kings shifted football's power balance, blaming BFF officials and club mafias for turf injuries and fixture manipulation.
Speed star Arifur Rahman has scored two goals in two straight matches for Chittagong Abahani.
Fan comments that finally someone dared to do something.
Fan looks back on 2021 without losing hope.
Fan shares semi-final poll votes and the Federation Cup quarter-final line-up for 2-3 January.
Fan is happy they will finally be able to watch the knockout stage matches.
Fan asks football lovers to take time to read a post.
Fan wishes everyone a happy new year.

incidents.title: Fans complain no channel shows Bangladesh matches as Asian Games go untelevised
incidents.summary: No TV channel or stream shows Bangladesh's Asian Games matches; fans ask if the country will ever get a sports channel. Suggested new category: broadcast_blackout.

incidents.title: Abahani humiliated in Bhutan as King's Cup campaign collapses
incidents.summary: Dhaka Abahani lose 1-0 to Bhutan's Ugyen Academy and stumble through the King's Cup in Bhutan; fans call it shameful and question why Abahani, not stronger clubs, were sent.

incidents.title: Fans protest foreign-player quota as Sheikh Jamal benches local stars
incidents.summary: Sheikh Jamal sign Jamal Bhuiyan on 350,000 taka a month yet bench local players while foreigners play; fans demand BFF limit foreigners to two registered and one in the XI. Suggested new category: foreign_player_quota.

incidents.title: De Kruif's future unknown as coach stays away before World Cup qualifiers
incidents.summary: Head coach Lodewijk de Kruif is not in Bangladesh for the Federation Cup or league and may not return for the qualifiers; only the goalkeeping coach turns up and BFF cannot say if he stays.

incidents.title: Fans ask if match fixing still exists after BFF-page comment on Sheikh Jamal
incidents.summary: A comment on the BFF page prompts fans to ask whether match fixing still exists in the league; a fan says Humayun's unproven claim was deleted but past fixing scandals involved Sheikh Jamal.

incidents.title: League confined to Dhaka as outstation venues are axed
incidents.summary: The professional league is organised on a single ground with clubs having no grounds of their own, and BFF axes all venues outside Dhaka except Chittagong.

incidents.title: Fans slam de Kruif's World Cup qualifier squad selections
incidents.summary: Fans erupt over the qualifier squad: Mishu, Hemanta, Toklis, Reza and Emon dropped while out-of-form Wahed, Sajib and Liton keep their places, and rumours say de Kruif prefers naturalised foreigners.

incidents.title: Rain postpones BPL matches as waterlogged pitch exposes drainage failure
incidents.summary: League matches are postponed by rain on a waterlogged Bangabandhu pitch fans photograph as a paddy field; BFF is told to fix the drainage before World Cup qualifiers.

incidents.title: Big clubs poach young stars then bench them, fans fear another Toklis/Rony case
incidents.summary: Shakhawat Rony loses his club and national place at Sheikh Jamal, then both Sheikh clubs chase young sensation Jewel Rana; fans fear another talent ruined by bench-warming. Suggested new category: talent_hoarding_benching.

incidents.title: Fitness crisis: 51 players injured after rushed BPL first leg
incidents.summary: Fifty-one players are injured after the rushed BPL first leg and fans demand BFF bring a trainer, physio and video analyst, warning fitness will cost the World Cup qualifiers.

incidents.title: Sheikh Jamal sack coach Maruful Haque after Abahani defeat
incidents.summary: Sheikh Jamal sack Maruful Haque, who says he was prepared to lose his job and blames foreign players who were not sincere in training.

incidents.title: Fans demand de Kruif sacked after winless World Cup qualifier start
incidents.summary: De Kruif admits he works a daily-wage, part-time job from Holland; after the Kyrgyzstan defeat and Tajikistan draw fans call for him and Titu to go, one post naming a players' syndicate and Dido's expulsion.

incidents.title: Fans turn on Zahid Hassan Emily as de Kruif keeps starting him
incidents.summary: Fans fume as Emily, unfit and missing chance after chance, stays in the XI while in-form Enamul is played out of position or benched; one post wishes him injured so the forward line changes.

incidents.title: BFF move to naturalise three African players splits fans
incidents.summary: Samad Yusuf, Ismail Bangoura and Kingsley Chigozie sign citizenship forms with BFF; ex-coach Manik calls citizenship too cheap and Alfaz Ahmed calls it a conspiracy, before BFF backs away and cancels the project under pressure. Suggested new category: foreign_player_naturalisation.

incidents.title: Clubs block national call-ups as BFF warn Sheikh Jamal
incidents.summary: Chittagong Abahani threaten U19 pick Shafayat Hossain Munna with suspension if he joins camp, Sheikh Jamal hold back Jamal Bhuyan and Mamunul from trials, and BFF vice-president Badal Roy warns of strict action.

incidents.title: No coaching staff scouting as Australia and Jordan qualifiers loom
incidents.summary: With Australia on 3 September, de Kruif is unwell, the goalkeeping coach is with Sheikh Jamal and assistant Titu is busy with the U19s, so nobody is scouting league players; fans note the ranking fell from 168 to 169 under Kruif.

incidents.title: Waterlogged pitches turn league matches into paddy-field football

entities.name: Sailor BFF National U-15 Football Championship

incidents.summary: League matches are played on muddy, waterlogged pitches fans call paddy fields, and BFF is warned the Bangabandhu pitch cannot survive the Jordan qualifier plus AFC U16 and U19 tournaments in the same month.

incidents.title: Farashganj suspended two years for giving a walkover
incidents.summary: Farashganj give a walkover and BFF suspend them from the Premier League for two years, fine them 5 lakh taka and order 13 lakh taka returned.

incidents.title: Expatriate hopefuls Akmol Ali and Rizwan Ahmed frozen out of national team
incidents.summary: Fans demand Akmol Ali and Rizwan Ahmed in the national team, call assistant coach Titu head of a syndicate panel, and ask how Akmol can play for Wales U19 yet fail Titu's fitness test.

incidents.title: De Kruif banned and fined, misses Australia dugout
incidents.summary: Four weeks before Australia, Kruif has still not come to Bangladesh; FIFA then ban him two matches and fine him 8,500 Swiss francs for indiscipline, and fans say a syndicate stopped him dropping players while BFF blocked stopping the league.

incidents.title: U16 SAFF champions neglected as AFC qualifiers expose grassroots gap
incidents.summary: A month after winning the SAFF U16 title, Bangladesh concede 11 goals to Saudi Arabia and the UAE in AFC qualifiers while India and Nepal qualify; fans say the talents will be lost and the half-dead BFF academy cannot even send food expenses on time. Suggested new category: youth_development_neglect.

incidents.title: Reasat Akmal frozen out as fans allege a selection syndicate
incidents.summary: Fans allege a syndicate keeps expatriate Reasat Akmal out while bench-warmers and Sajib walk into the squad, pointing to top-scorer lists where Enamul sits on the bench and Emily starts automatically.

incidents.title: Fans slam Titu's defensive tactics as U19s crash out of SAFF and AFC qualifiers
incidents.summary: Titu's five-defender, park-the-bus tactics are blamed for the SAFF U19 semi-final exit to India and the AFC U19 failure against Bhutan and Uzbekistan; BFF say he will never again head-coach a national team.

incidents.title: No channel shows Bangladesh's Australia qualifier as TV blackout returns
incidents.summary: Channels show the English Premier League and Indian Super League but not Bangladesh's World Cup qualifiers against Australia and Kyrgyzstan; fans demand a protest. Suggested new category: broadcast_blackout.

incidents.title: BFF sack de Kruif in salary row and appoint Fabio Lopez
incidents.summary: De Kruif refuses to coach in Australia over unpaid salary, BFF pay 70 percent then decide to sack him; on leaving he says officials interfered in team selection and broke promises, and BFF appoint Italy's Fabio Lopez on 15,000 dollars a month.

incidents.title: Australia tour shame: hotel misconduct claims and nameless jerseys
incidents.summary: In Perth the team are accused of misbehaving at their hotel, Tim Cahill refuses Mamunul's jersey because it carries no name, flag or country, and fans find the kit is made by GoalBangladesh with Lotto socks.

incidents.title: Expatriate players Reasat, Akmol, Rizwan and Faruke still frozen out after Kruif exit
incidents.summary: Fans say Rizwan, Akmol and Faruke will never wear the jersey now Kruif, who searched for them, is gone; Reasat is called the national team's most valuable player on Transfermarkt yet has no place.

incidents.title: Sheikh Kamal Gold Cup organisation unravels before kick-off
incidents.summary: League runners-up Sheikh Russel are not invited, Mohun Bagan pull out, organisers do not know all the teams days before kick-off, champions Sheikh Jamal and Russel are absent, and Chittagong Abahani field a borrowed team beyond loan limits while fans ask why 8-10 crore taka is spent on it.

incidents.title: Hemanta Vincent dropped for playing khep matches while injured
incidents.summary: Hemanta plays unauthorised khep matches in Dinajpur while claiming injury and missing national camp; Lopez drops him from the preliminary squad and BFF dither over giving him another chance.

incidents.title: Eid congregation held on BFF turf, ruining the pitch
incidents.summary: BFF allow an Eid jamaat on the new turf, which fans say ruins the expensive ground they waited years for.

incidents.title: Lopez's positional experiments unsettle senior players
incidents.summary: New coach Lopez plays Mamunul out of position, Rony in midfield and Faisal Mahmud at right-back; Mamunul says he is uncomfortable and cannot play his best, and players complain publicly instead of to the coach.

incidents.title: Fixing alert: fans demand investigation after Daily Star report
incidents.summary: A Daily Star fixing alert prompts fans to recall the 2009 Bangladesh-Nepal match as possibly fixed and Nepal's players taking 1,000 dollars to fix internationals; one post says a Bangladesh fixing investigation would sink many big club and federation people.

incidents.title: Sheikh Jamal president Manjur Kader takes on BFF over Cup exclusion
incidents.summary: After Sheikh Jamal are excluded from the Sheikh Kamal Cup, president Manjur Kader calls Salahuddin spineless and incompetent, secret election meetings plot against the president, clubs threaten to force the Super Cup and Independence Cup, and Kader and Lokman Bhuiyan are show-caused for meeting players before a match.

incidents.title: BCB take MA Aziz Stadium for cricket as Chittagong football loses its ground
incidents.summary: Chittagong fans demand a full football ground at MA Aziz Stadium, then BCB take it for the cricket BPL over the better-equipped Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium; BFF are blamed for letting Bangabandhu Stadium fall into neglect while BCB maintain their grounds.

incidents.title: Zahid Hossain dropped for fitness and discipline as he plays on for Chittagong Abahani
incidents.summary: Lopez says Zahid and Emily are not fit for the national team, yet Zahid scores a hat-trick for Chittagong Abahani; fans accuse him of faking injury and skipping fitness training, and he then declines a late national call-up.

incidents.title: Naturalisation debate revived before SAFF as expatriate route is argued instead
incidents.summary: Fans renew the call to naturalise Bangoura, Kingsley, Wedson and Emeka for SAFF, while a Prothom Alo column argues BFF should scout expatriate Bangladeshis like Jamal Bhuyan and Joseph Nur Rahman instead. Suggested new category: foreign_player_naturalisation.

incidents.title: Fans demand Lopez sacked after winless start, BFF sack him and appoint Maruful
incidents.summary: After a draw with second-division Arambagh and defeats to a Myanmar club side, a Chinese club and Tajikistan 5-0, fans chant #lopez_out; BFF sack Lopez on 24 November and appoint Maruful Haque, and Wali Faisal says Lopez told him a local coach had told him not to pick him.

incidents.title: Sheikh Jamal transfer war: dues row, league and AFC boycott threats, president Kader's resignation
incidents.summary: Sheikh Jamal's 1.44-crore dues row escalated into a transfer war with league and AFC Cup boycott threats, ending with club president Manjur Kader's resignation.

incidents.title: Sylhet Academy closes within a year after FIFA's 700,000 dollars
incidents.summary: The Sylhet Academy, launched with FIFA's 700,000 dollars and costing a crore a year to run, closes within a year with no sponsor or budget.

incidents.title: Age-fraud culture exposed as overage players are sent to U13 tournaments
incidents.summary: Fans ask why 17-18-year-olds are sent in U13 teams and mock the age-fraud culture in which overage sides beat Ronaldinho's Brazil and Dinamo Zagreb at the Mokh Cup yet the same generation fails AFC U16 qualifiers.

incidents.title: National team players get no contract, salary or injury support in camp
incidents.summary: SAFF camp food is worse than under the previous foreign coaches with Jamal in hospital, and fans ask what players get in camp: no central contract, no salary or injury support, poor food and no proper gym despite a reported 6 crore taka spent on the team.

incidents.title: Bangabandhu Gold Cup downgraded as teams send youth squads
incidents.summary: Defending champions Malaysia balk at the January Bangabandhu Gold Cup and Bahrain and Maldives send U21 squads instead of national teams.

incidents.title: SAFF 2015 organisation descends into chaos in Kerala
incidents.summary: Mismanagement begins at the SAFF Suzuki Cup in Kerala: no practice grounds or buses, six-hour hotel check-ins, Nepal taken to the wrong Taj hotel, Bangladesh players two to a bed, and a 5,000-rupee charge for a meeting room.

incidents.title: Attack on BFF office halts Championship and third-division leagues
incidents.summary: The Professional League Committee suspend the Championship League until further notice in protest at the attack on the BFF office, then third-division football is stopped too. Suggested new category: attack_on_federation_office.

incidents.title: SAFF exit exposes grouping and fights inside the national team
incidents.summary: After the SAFF group-stage exit, an Alokito report describes a Sheikh Jamal group and a rising-players group inside the team, Jamal pushing Yeasin who throws punches back in the Bhutan match, and fans demand Babu's sacking, a probe and lifetime bans, while ex-players say Salahuddin should resign. Suggested new category: player_grouping_syndicate.

incidents.title: Maruful Haque's future uncertain after SAFF exit
incidents.summary: Fans plead not to sack Maruf after the SAFF exit and ask to keep him till March, then breaking news says he will not stay even after BFF's offer, before BFF keep him for the Bangabandhu Gold Cup with no contract length stated.

incidents.title: Fans plan human-chain protest outside BFF after SAFF exit
incidents.summary: Supporters propose a human chain in front of the BFF building on Saturday 2 January at 3pm with banners from all football groups to save football, ending with a memorandum in English since Salahuddin does not read Bangla.

incidents.title: National players play paid 'khep' exhibitions after SAFF failure
incidents.summary: Captain Mamunul Islam and most national players played paid 'khep' exhibition matches in Narayanganj days after returning from SAFF, days before Bangabandhu Gold Cup reporting; fans split between condemning the indiscipline and defending players who need the money.

incidents.title: SAFF failure inquiry blames indiscipline; seven players show-caused amid drug claims

entities.name: Sheikh Mohammad Aslam
entities.role: former player / BFF executive committee member

incidents.summary: BFF's SAFF failure inquiry, led by Sheikh Mohammad Aslam, blamed indiscipline above all; Aslam publicly claimed players were drug addicts with no discipline, and seven footballers including captain Mamunul were served show-cause notices.

incidents.title: Sheikh Mohammad Aslam resigns from BFF executive committee

entities.name: Sheikh Mohammad Aslam
entities.role: former player / BFF executive committee member

incidents.summary: Former national striker Sheikh Mohammad Aslam resigned from BFF's executive committee, saying he joined dreaming of developing football but could not do any work in the committee.

incidents.title: Mamunul and Zahid banned a year, Sohel and Yeasin six months for indiscipline
incidents.summary: BFF banned captain Mamunul Islam and Zahid Hossain from the national team for one year and Sohel Rana and Yeasin Khan for six months for indiscipline; Mamunul called it an injustice he could not accept.

incidents.title: Sheikh Jamal's AFC Cup and Independence Cup flip-flopping ends in court
incidents.summary: Sheikh Jamal kept reversing its stance on the AFC Cup and Independence Cup over its missing players, BFF sent national players to Magura instead of releasing them for the AFC Cup, and a court ordered eight players back to Jamal, rebuking them for taking money from another club while contracted.

incidents.title: Refereeing row in Sheikh Jamal's 4-3 AFC Cup loss to Selangor
incidents.summary: Fans said the referee denied Sheikh Jamal two clear penalties, including a handball inside the box, in the 4-3 AFC Cup home defeat to Selangor FA.

incidents.title: Refereeing complaints in Jordan's 8-0 World Cup qualifier win
incidents.summary: Fans blamed poor refereeing, including a wrongly awarded corner leading to a goal and harsh penalties, in Bangladesh's 8-0 World Cup qualifier defeat in Jordan.

incidents.title: BFF election 2016: vote-buying, huge costs and fear of a FIFA ban
incidents.summary: The 30 April 2016 BFF election drew claims that president and vice-president posts cost 1.5-2 crore taka to contest and councillors' votes were bought for 10-20 lakh, with Salahuddin's manifesto read out in his absence and fears the election chaos could bring a FIFA ban.

incidents.title: De Kruif returns on a one-month contract with banned players recalled
incidents.summary: Lodewijk de Kruif returned as national coach on a one-month contract for the Tajikistan Asian Cup qualifier, with the banned footballers brought back into the fold.

incidents.title: Sheikh Jamal decide not to play the 2017 AFC Cup
incidents.summary: After the season-long dispute with BFF, Sheikh Jamal decided not to enter the 2017 AFC Cup, letting the entry deadline pass despite qualifying as league champions.

incidents.title: Federation Cup: officials and ball boy assault referees after controversial goals
incidents.summary: After controversial refereeing in Federation Cup quarter-finals, Brothers Union officials, a ball boy and an assistant manager physically assaulted the referee and assistant, and Rahmatganj officials also laid hands on a referee; BFF later banned a Brothers footballer for a year.

incidents.title: Saintfiet on Nigeria's coaching shortlist; fans fear he will leave
incidents.summary: Tom Saintfiet appeared on the three-man shortlist for the Nigeria head coach job, and fans worried Bangladesh would lose him, noting his family and agent had not wanted him to come to Bangladesh.

incidents.title: Clubs refuse seven BPL venues and will play at four
incidents.summary: Clubs refused to play the Premier League at seven venues outside Dhaka and insisted on four, despite crores spent taking the league outside the capital; sponsors threatened to withdraw if venues were cut.

incidents.title: Nepotism alleged in Saintfiet's preliminary squad for Bhutan
incidents.summary: Fans alleged nepotism after BFF announced a 33-member preliminary squad for Bhutan without discussing it with coach Saintfiet, including bench-warming and out-of-form players at the preference of federation officials, with two reserve-bench players reportedly pushed by a national-team official.

incidents.title: BPL grounds likened to paddy fields
incidents.summary: Fans condemned the state of Premier League grounds, describing them as paddy fields with long grass and slow surfaces despite budget and time to improve them.

incidents.title: Mamunul 'syndicate' and group politics before the Bhutan tie
incidents.summary: Fans accused captain Mamunul Islam of running a syndicate and group politics in the national team, driving coaches out and creating conflict, after he came out of retirement for the Bhutan tie; others defended him as the only midfield option.

incidents.title: Tom Saintfiet resigns as national coach
incidents.summary: Tom Saintfiet resigned as Bangladesh coach and left Dhaka, after publicly criticising BFF's professionalism, the lack of fit players and no trainer being appointed over budget, and advising BFF to work at grassroots level.

incidents.title: Bhutan 3-1 elimination sparks Salahuddin resignation demands and street protest
incidents.summary: Bangladesh's 3-1 defeat to Bhutan in the Asian Cup pre-qualifiers, which fans said would bar the team from FIFA tournaments for three years, triggered demands for Kazi Salahuddin and the whole BFF committee to resign and a small street protest.

incidents.title: Bangladesh withdraw from the AFC Solidarity Cup despite a $20,000 fine
incidents.summary: BFF decided not to send the national team to the 2016 AFC Solidarity Cup, preferring to rebuild for the next SAFF, even though withdrawal meant a $20,000 FIFA fine; fans noted Nepal took Bangladesh's place in the Asian Cup qualifiers as Solidarity Cup champions.

incidents.title: BFF officials alleged to have bought flats worth Tk 1.2 crore
incidents.summary: Posts alleged some people working in the football federation had bought flats for Tk 1.2 crore and booked another, asking why the Anti-Corruption Commission said nothing.

incidents.title: FIFA grant suspended and Nepal's Bangabandhu Gold Cup prize money unpaid
incidents.summary: FIFA suspended its financial grant to BFF and BFF still had not paid Nepal's Bangabandhu Gold Cup champions' prize money; a later audit report had shown all dues including prize money as paid, though the money was never handed over.

incidents.title: Relegation play-off row: BFF accused of trying to save Feni and Uttar Baridhara
incidents.summary: After Feni Soccer and Uttar Baridhara finished level on points, BFF mentioned a two-legged relegation play-off, and fans shared rumours that BFF was trying to save both clubs from relegation despite refusing to play.

incidents.title: BFF withdraw from the Women's Asian Cup qualifiers
incidents.summary: BFF withdrew the women's national team from the AFC Women's Asian Cup qualifiers while spending hugely on the Bangabandhu Gold Cup and Sheikh Kamal Cup, drawing praise for the girls and blame for the federation.

incidents.title: BFF general secretary Shohag accused of harassing an employee
incidents.summary: An Ekattor TV report said a BFF employee was harassed, blaming general secretary Abu Nayeem Shohag, and fans asked whether Shohag was absconding. Suggested new category: federation official misconduct.

incidents.title: Andrew Ord hiring confusion and salary disagreement
incidents.summary: BFF was close to signing British-Australian Andrew Ord but could not agree on salary, amid confusion over his coaching experience and an emergency meeting that ignored the most urgent issue.

incidents.title: Bangabandhu Stadium press box glass shattered in storm, repairs promised but not done
incidents.summary: A storm broke the Bangabandhu National Stadium press box glass wall, leaving journalists suffering in the heat despite promises of repair.

incidents.title: BPL sponsorship collapses from Tk 4 crore to Tk 1.5 crore
incidents.summary: Sponsorship money for the Premier League fell from Tk 4 crore to Tk 1.5 crore, with league owner Saif Global Sports struggling to find sponsors. Suggested new category: league sponsorship / commercial crisis.

incidents.title: U-23 humiliated 0-7 by Jordan; renewed calls to remove Salahuddin and the BFF panel
incidents.summary: Bangladesh U-23 lost 0-7 to Jordan in the AFC U-23 qualifiers and went on to lose all three games; fans repeated calls to remove Salahuddin and the entire BFF panel, accused BFF of deleting dissenting comments, and shared Ord's and Rupu's assessments of the failed campaign.

incidents.title: BPL played on monsoon muddy grounds
incidents.summary: Fans asked why the league was started in the monsoon on waterlogged grounds fit for paddy cultivation, with bad drainage at the venues.

incidents.title: Over-aged players alleged in age-group teams
incidents.summary: Fans accused BFF of again calling over-aged players to age-group teams, questioned whether the U-15 and U-18 sides were really their stated ages, and noted Bangladesh had won the SAFF U-16 with age cheating; one post warned FIFA could ban Bangladesh if age cheating was proven.

incidents.title: U-16 women's team prepared against school teams, then lost 9-0 to North Korea

entities.name: North Korea U-16 women's national team

incidents.summary: BFF arranged preparation matches for the U-16 women's team against Chinese and Korean school teams instead of strong sides; the girls then lost 9-0 to North Korea, with fans blaming the turf switch, morning practice and weak preparation.

incidents.title: #Salauddin_out and #Save_Bangladesh_Football protest wave
incidents.summary: Fans ran a #Salauddin_out and #Save_Bangladesh_Football protest across BFF's page and TV channels' pages, calling for a social mass awakening to save football.

incidents.title: Refereeing row in Bangladesh U-16's 0-2 loss to Yemen
incidents.summary: Fans blamed the referee for Bangladesh U-16's 0-2 AFC U-16 Championship loss to Yemen, saying the first goal came from a clear dive for a penalty and the second was a 50/50 offside.

incidents.title: Sabina Yasmin dies; U-15 women's camp had no doctor or health checks
incidents.summary: Teenage U-15 women's footballer Sabina Yasmin (Kolsindur) died of a slight fever before joining the camp; fans asked why there was no doctor or health check at camp and why she could not afford primary treatment, and a later Prothom Alo piece marked her missing the title from the other side. Note: two fan posts in this cluster misname her 'Sabina Khatun' — the senior women's star, a different person.

incidents.title: Aminul Haque's English league dream shattered by BFF indifference
incidents.summary: The dream of the first Bangladeshi playing in the English league was shattered by BFF officials' indifference and communication problems, in a story about Aminul Haque. Suggested new category: federation negligence blocking a player opportunity.

incidents.title: AFC result page error: Bangladesh shown as winners, then deleted
incidents.summary: The AFC wrote Bangladesh as winners on the U-19 qualifiers result page and then deleted it, while its match report claimed Maldives won by Sufil's own goal; fans said everything could be edited and the AFC had admitted it.

incidents.title: Brunei's last-minute withdrawal alleged to be fixing
incidents.summary: Brunei, notorious for regularly withdrawing from continental tournaments, withdrew one day before the group games, which the poster said they would never rule out as fixing.

incidents.title: Bangabandhu Stadium ground in terrible state
incidents.summary: The Bangabandhu National Stadium ground was in such a terrible state that even Cambodia and Laos had far better grounds and passing football was impossible there.

incidents.title: Emeka Ezeugo's $22,000 dues unpaid; BFF risk FIFA action
incidents.summary: BFF could not pay former Mohammedan coach Emeka Ezeugo's $22,000 arrears by the deadline, so he could go to FIFA again; Emeka said he loved Mohammedan but bad people sank it and blamed BFF.

incidents.title: Farashganj and Rahmatganj relegation matches alleged fixed; Kamal Babu accused of asking Saif to concede
incidents.summary: Fans allege Farashganj's 3-1 win over Sheikh Jamal and Rahmatganj's win were fixed to escape relegation, and that coach Kamal Babu asked Saif to concede a match.

incidents.title: AFC unhappy with Bangladeshi professional football; clubs called 'merely a group'
incidents.summary: AFC licensing demands at least six venues and its representative calls Bangladeshi clubs 'merely a group', with Sheikh Jamal and Chittagong Abahani kept out of the AFC Cup.

incidents.title: Abahani's AFC Cup failure blamed on coach Saiful Bari Titu's defensive tactics
incidents.summary: Fans furiously criticise Abahani coach Titu's negative, defensive tactics through the 2018 AFC Cup campaign, questioning his appointment and excuses after heavy defeats.

incidents.title: BFF joins Saudi-led SWAFF alliance; Bangladesh's share of its money hidden
incidents.summary: BFF joins the Saudi-led SWAFF alliance and fans ask where Bangladesh's reported $500,000 annual share went, as the AFC seeks an explanation from BFF.

incidents.title: BFF vice-president Badal Roy in conflict with general secretary Abu Nayeem Shohag
incidents.summary: BFF vice-president Badal Roy's wife alleges general secretary Shohag threatened the family and files a general diary, exposing an open BFF leadership conflict.

incidents.title: SAFF 2018 venue not ready: floodlights, broken galleries and no promotion
incidents.summary: With SAFF 2018 returning to Dhaka, fans report Bangabandhu Stadium's floodlights not raised to standard, broken galleries and no promotion from organiser BFF.

incidents.title: SAFF 2018 squad: Jafar Iqbal and Matin Mia omitted, 'lobbying politics' blamed
incidents.summary: Fans protest the SAFF 2018 squad omitting in-form Jafar Iqbal and Matin Mia while Roni and Faisal Mahmud are picked, blaming lobbying and the Abahani quota.

incidents.title: After SAFF exit, fans demand Salahuddin and Rupu resign; Rupu threatens a journalist
incidents.summary: After Bangladesh crash out of SAFF 2018 at home, fans flood the group demanding Salahuddin, Rupu and other officials resign, and Rupu is reported to have threatened Ekattor TV journalist Saiful Rupok over a story on goalkeeper Sohel's inclusion.

incidents.title: Women's team success unrewarded; male manager and Paul Smalley questioned
incidents.summary: Fans ask why the successful women's team gets no protection or rewards, questioning a male manager in the women's team, technical director Paul Smalley, and BFF's neglect.

incidents.title: Bangabandhu Gold Cup: Saad Uddin dropped after road accident, Matin Mia benched
incidents.summary: Saad Uddin is dropped after a road accident and Matin Mia pleads for even a minute at the home Bangabandhu Gold Cup, fuelling claims Jamie Day and Rupu freeze out non-quota players.

incidents.title: Badal Roy demands BFF president Salahuddin resign
incidents.summary: BFF vice-president Badal Roy publicly demands president Kazi Salahuddin resign, the open leadership split reaching television.

incidents.title: Nasir's token-money row: clubs appeal, one-year ban threatened
incidents.summary: Abahani, Rahmatganj and BJMC appeal to the Players' Status Committee over Nasir's token money, and Nasir faces a one-year ban if he cannot settle with Abahani in three days.

incidents.title: Referees 'influenced' by BFF officials standing in dugouts as club managers
incidents.summary: Fans argue referees cannot be neutral while BFF officials double as club and national-team managers in the dugout, citing decisions against Mohammedan and Arambagh.

incidents.title: BFF academy saga: 5.5 crore taka FIFA grant unspent, Sylhet BKSP academy closed
incidents.summary: BFF's Sylhet BKSP academy closes after nearly 5.5 crore taka of FIFA grant is not spent on it, fans ask where the money went, and Salahuddin promises an academy by 1 March.

incidents.title: Anti-Corruption Commission summons BFF president Salahuddin
incidents.summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission summons Kazi Salahuddin over irregularity and embezzlement allegations, alongside listed unpaid players, coach and camp supplier claims.

incidents.title: Kiron corruption row: arrest warrant, 167 foreign trips, 4.5 crore taka
incidents.summary: BFF women's chief Mahfuza Akter Kiron faces a five-part TV investigation, an arrest warrant over 167 foreign trips costing about 4.5 crore taka while the women's league stayed closed, then jail and bail.

incidents.title: Match-fixing 'in discussion again' in the league
incidents.summary: A widely shared report says match-fixing is in discussion again in Bangladeshi football (single high-engagement post).

incidents.title: Bangamata Gold Cup: weak opponents, 600-taka gloves, women's league closed six years
incidents.summary: Fans call the Bangamata U-19 a staged showpiece with weak opponents, note the girls get 600-taka gloves in a crore-taka tournament, and that the women's league has been closed for six years with BJMC hinting at shutting its women's team.

incidents.title: World Cup pre-qualifier neglected: no camp, no squad, Jamie Day absent
incidents.summary: While rivals announce squads and start camps for the World Cup pre-qualifier against Laos, BFF has no squad or camp, Jamie Day has not arrived, and fans blame obsession with the Bangamata showpiece tournament.

incidents.title: Abahani goalkeeper Sohel's repeated AFC Cup errors, yet still selected
incidents.summary: Sohel's mistakes cost Abahani AFC Cup matches, yet fans note he is played repeatedly by Abahani and then picked for the national team.

incidents.title: Bangabandhu Stadium drainage fails; league broadcasts unwatchable
incidents.summary: BNS has no super-sopper and a sunken drainage system, water is removed by spades, and league broadcasts are so poor players look like ants, while Noakhali's field still has no grass.

incidents.title: Mohammedan's destruction blamed on Babu, Lokman and Emily
incidents.summary: A high-engagement post names Mohammedan manager Amirul Islam Babu, Lokman Hossain Bhuiyan and Zahid Hassan Emily as the men behind Mohammedan's destruction. Suggested new category: club_mismanagement.

incidents.title: Laos squad: Toklis and Yasin Arafat ignored, Mamunul picked
incidents.summary: Fans protest the Laos preliminary squad leaving out two-goal Toklis and 19-year-old Yasin Arafat while Mamunul, who scores one, is picked.

incidents.title: Jibon labelled a 'Rupu-quota' forward with zero goals in 12 internationals
incidents.summary: Fans label Nabib Newaj Jibon a Rupu-quota forward with no goals in his last 12 internationals, mocking his missed chances and questioning why in-form strikers sit out.

incidents.title: Yasin Khan excluded for 15 matches after staying loyal to Sheikh Jamal
incidents.summary: Fans protest Yasin Khan's exclusion from the national squad for 15 matches, saying it punishes him for staying loyal to Sheikh Jamal during the BFF-Monzur Kader rivalry (single high-engagement post).

incidents.title: Captain Jamal Bhuyan says referees give Abahani 'special facilities'; BFF show-causes him
incidents.summary: Captain Jamal Bhuyan says referees give one team, Abahani, special facilities, and BFF show-causes him for the criticism instead of addressing the refereeing.

incidents.title: Mohammedan left out of Sheikh Kamal Cup while Kolkata Mohammedan invited
incidents.summary: Dhaka Mohammedan, the country's most popular club, is not invited to the Sheikh Kamal Cup while third-tier Kolkata Mohammedan is, which fans call broker management.

incidents.title: Jamie Day 'lacks courage to break Rupu's syndicate' as World Cup qualifiers falter
incidents.summary: Fans say Jamie Day takes too much holiday, plays fearfully with long throws, and lacks the courage to break Rupu's syndicate, blaming him equally for quota selections in the World Cup qualifiers.

incidents.title: National-team fitness divide: some players 'drink alcohol and ganja yet stay in the team'
incidents.summary: A high-engagement post alleges a fitness divide in the national team, claiming some players drink alcohol and ganja yet stay in the team while fitter players are overlooked; allegation only, unverified (single high-engagement post).

incidents.title: Casino crackdown reaches football: Lokman's Mohammedan casino, 'Casino World Cup' jibes
incidents.summary: After the casino raids, fans demand Lokman and Babu be thrown out of Mohammedan for life, detail Lokman renting the club's place for a casino, and joke Salahuddin's Vision-2022 meant the Casino World Cup.

incidents.title: Sheikh Kamal Cup: referee allegedly racially abuses Chennai City player
incidents.summary: A Sri Lankan referee allegedly makes a racist comment to a Chennai City player in the Sheikh Kamal Cup game against Bashundhara Kings, and Chennai complain to the match commissioner.

incidents.title: Bashundhara Kings vs BFF: official 'going room to room' in national camp, release row
incidents.summary: Kings president Imrul Hassan says an official goes room to room in the national-team camp telling players to play for a specific club, as Kings refuse early release of players and fans note no club manager in the world is also national-team manager.

incidents.title: Women's team not sent to the SA Games
incidents.summary: Fans criticise BFF for not sending a women's team to the SA Games, tracing it to Salahuddin refusing to play the Bangamata final against Laos, while Jibon is picked as a senior SA Games quota player over Rakib and Sufil.

incidents.title: SA Games failure: Jamie Day's long-ball tactics and love for Jibon mocked
incidents.summary: After the SA Games loss, fans mock Jamie Day's long-ball tactics, his refusal to rotate the failing Jibon, and Rupu's interference in the team.

incidents.title: Kiron's two-league plan and FIFA earnings questioned as 2019 ends
incidents.summary: Mahfuza Akter Kiron wants to run two seasons' leagues at once in 2020 after failing to run one in six years, and fans note she earns about $3.5 lakh a year from FIFA Council and AFC roles, as Salahuddin calls 2019 a successful year.

incidents.title: FIFA fines BFF after spectators invade pitch in World Cup qualifier
incidents.summary: FIFA fines the BFF about 13 lakh taka after spectators climbed the wall and entered the field during a World Cup qualifier.

incidents.title: Saif Sporting Club sack coach Mohammad Nizam after two months
incidents.summary: Saif appoint Maldives coach Mohammad Nizam in November and sack him just two months later.

incidents.title: Rupu's grip on national-team selection during the Bangabandhu Gold Cup
incidents.summary: Fans accuse team manager Satyajit Das Rupu of keeping favourites Mamunul Islam and Raihan Hasan in the XI while shutting out in-form players, as Bangladesh exit the Bangabandhu Gold Cup.

incidents.title: Tarafder Ruhul Amin withdraws from the BFF presidential race
incidents.summary: Salahuddin's main rival Tarafder Ruhul Amin steps back three months before the BFF election after years of preparation, prompting accusations of a backroom deal and fans bidding football farewell.

incidents.title: Calls to sack Saiful Bari Titu
incidents.summary: Fans call for coach Saiful Bari Titu's removal after a run of draws and a slide towards the relegation zone.

incidents.title: Tariq Kazi, the most high-profile Bangladeshi-origin player, left out of the national team
incidents.summary: Fans ask why Tariq Kazi, with Europa League qualifiers and Finnish top-tier experience, is not in the national team.

incidents.title: Dreams of 23 women footballers who left home for Dhaka under threat
incidents.summary: The dreams of 23 women footballers who left their families for Dhaka are reported to be under threat.

incidents.title: Sheikh Kamal Club Cup champions still unpaid months later
incidents.summary: Terengganu FC, champions of last October's Sheikh Kamal International Club Cup, still have not received their prize money, and fans accuse BFF of insulting the tournament's namesake.

incidents.title: Oscar Bruzon plays players out of position at Bashundhara Kings
incidents.summary: Kings coach Oscar Bruzon is accused of playing forwards in defence and defenders in midfield, with the whole team passing only to Daniel Colindres.

incidents.title: Biased refereeing in the league
incidents.summary: Fans accuse referees of deciding matches, including making Abahani win and blowing the whistle in Bashundhara Kings' favour.

incidents.title: Abahani keep playing flop Sunday Chizoba while benching Faisal Shitlu
incidents.summary: Fans demand Abahani drop Sunday Chizoba, goalless in many matches, and give a chance to Faisal Shitlu, who won them an important match last year.

incidents.title: Badal Roy alleges Salahuddin wants to run the BFF election mafia-style
incidents.summary: Former Mohammedan and national star Badal Roy alleges in Prothom Alo that Salahuddin wants to run the BFF election in mafia style.

incidents.title: Cumilla venue pitch injury-prone ahead of league and AFC Cup matches
incidents.summary: Photos show the Cumilla venue in poor, injury-prone condition the day before Mohammedan face Bashundhara Kings there and Kings play an AFC Cup match.

incidents.title: BFF give top-scorer award to a player seven goals behind the top scorer
incidents.summary: Suggested new category: award irregularity. BFF give the best award to a player who scored seven fewer goals than the top scorer on 20 goals in a pipeline tournament.

incidents.title: Fans demand an audit of BFF officials' assets
incidents.summary: Fans call the BFF leadership the great destroyers of Bangla football and say an audit of all their assets would clear up a lot.

incidents.title: Jamal Bhuyan recalls the syndicate inside the national team at his 2011 trial
incidents.summary: Jamal Bhuyan recalls his first trial in Bangladesh in 2011, when he became a laughing stock and saw the terrible syndicate within the team before returning to Denmark.

incidents.title: Over-age players hidden in the Pioneer League
incidents.summary: Nepotism spreads to hiding players' ages in the Pioneer League, where over-15 players escape officials' notice.

incidents.title: Turf pitches injuring young players
incidents.summary: Players and fans blame turf pitches for injuries, with BFF citing FIFA research while a defender says the heavy ground hurt his leg muscles and Saif's youth train at Kamalapur's injury mine.

incidents.title: Injured Jony: FIFA paid for recovery, BFF never checks on him
incidents.summary: Suggested new category: player welfare neglect. FIFA gave injured Masuk Mia Jony 4 lakh taka for recovery and Bashundhara paid him in full, but he is disappointed BFF does not check on him regularly.

incidents.title: BFF executive committee serves extra time after its term expires
incidents.summary: BFF's executive committee term ends on 30 April, yet the committee led by Kazi Salahuddin keeps serving extra time with FIFA's approval.

incidents.title: FIFA ban Saif Sporting Club from transfers over $130,000 unpaid to foreign players
incidents.summary: FIFA instruct BFF to ban Saif Sporting Club from all transfers for not paying $130,000 to three foreign players.

incidents.title: FIFA and government academy money taken, no academy built in 12 years
incidents.summary: Fans note BFF spent over 100 crore in four years while Salahuddin is accused of taking FIFA and government money for an academy and lying about it for a dozen years, as poorer Nepal builds three academies.

incidents.title: BPL cancelled with no champion, no promotion or relegation, and AFC slots at risk
incidents.summary: Clubs tell BFF they do not want to play the league, which is cancelled with no champion named, no promotion or relegation, players unconsulted, and Bangladesh at risk of losing an AFC slot.

incidents.title: Age fraud in SAFF age-group football is not new
incidents.summary: Age fraud in age-group football is described as long-running in Bangladesh, driven by hopes of shortcut success, citing recent SAFF age-group tournaments.

incidents.title: Syndicate admissions: Emily says he picked Mamunul and Jahid when given team-building power
